ops.name: anim.additive
ops.summary: An additive copy of an animation (it then layers on top of whatever plays under it in Sequencer: a gesture or
ops.doc:
An additive copy of an animation (it then layers on top of whatever plays under it in Sequencer: a gesture or
a breath over an idle or a walk, without replacing the legs).

Args: anim: the source. out: the additive copy's path (re-made on each call). base: what is subtracted:
"first_frame" (the clip's own frame `frame`: the usual for a gesture authored from a rest pose), "ref_pose"
(the skeleton's reference pose), or an AnimSequence path (its frame `frame`). space: "local" or "mesh"
(rotation offset in mesh space: aiming layers).
Returns: {"out", "changed": true, "type", "base"}.
Example: film-ue op anim.additive anim=/Game/Anim/AS_Shrug out=/Game/Anim/AS_Shrug_Add

ops.name: anim.bake_follow
ops.summary: Make a follower animation (a MetaHuman face's) carry its leader's pose: bake_pose from the leader (the body)
ops.doc:
Make a follower animation (a MetaHuman face's) carry its leader's pose: bake_pose from the leader (the body)
into `out` for every non-facial bone the two skeletons share, and switch the face rig's own head control off
(headcontrolswitch 0) unless `head_control`, so the head turns only as the body's does. A face playing alone
otherwise keeps its neck and chest apart from the body, and its chest pokes through the clothes. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op anim.bake_follow sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 actor_label=Presenter anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1 out=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1_follow

ops.name: anim.bake_pose
ops.summary: Sample `source` (a skeletal mesh component of the actor) as it really plays in `sequence` (animation, rig and
ops.doc:
Sample `source` (a skeletal mesh component of the actor) as it really plays in `sequence` (animation, rig and
post-process correctives included) and write those bones, local to their parents, as bone tracks into `out` (a
copy of `anim`), which then goes on `target`'s track. Keys past the sequence keep the animation's own pose; curves
are untouched. A multi-tick job.
Example: film-ue op anim.bake_pose sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 actor_label=Presenter source=Body target=Face anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1 out=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1_baked 'bones=["neck_01","head"]'

ops.name: anim.body_life
ops.summary: An additive animation of body life for a body skeleton: breathing (spine extension and clavicle lift on each
ops.doc:
An additive animation of body life for a body skeleton: breathing (spine extension and clavicle lift on each
inhale, at a rate by `state`: calm, rest, listen, talk, focus, nervous), slow weight shifts (`shift_cm` of pelvis,
the spine bending back over the feet) and, with `face_anim`, the torso following the head's turns (`follow` of
its yaw, a beat later). Layer it over any idle: seq.anim with replace=false, or a spec's character.body_life.
Needs perf.calibrate_body for this skeleton.

Args: out: the additive animation's path (re-made). body_mesh: the body SkeletalMesh. length_s: seconds.
face_anim: a face animation whose HeadYaw the torso follows. Others: amplitudes in degrees / cm.
Returns: {"out", "changed", "breaths_per_min", "shifts", "bones"}.
Example: film-ue op anim.body_life out=/Game/Perf/AS_life body_mesh=/Game/MetaHumans/Ada/Body/m_med_nrw_body length_s=12 state=talk

ops.name: anim.check
ops.summary: Will this face read as alive? Numeric naturalness checks on an animation's curves (perfkit.metrics): frozen
ops.doc:
Will this face read as alive? Numeric naturalness checks on an animation's curves (perfkit.metrics): frozen
head, linear (robotic) head moves, head jitter, blink rate/regularity/shape, left-right asymmetry, upper-face
range, gaze activity. Each check {"name", "pass", "metric", "threshold", "why"}.

Args: anim: a face animation (MetaHuman face curves). signs: perf.calibrate's result (rig signs/eye gains).
Returns: {"pass", "failed": [names], "checks": [...], "blinks": {...}}.
Example: film-ue op anim.check anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1

ops.name: anim.curve
ops.summary: One curve's keys (every n-th): times and values, with its range.
ops.doc:
One curve's keys (every n-th): times and values, with its range.
Example: film-ue op anim.curve anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1 name=HeadYaw

ops.name: anim.curves
ops.summary: A sequence's float curve names (containing `contains`).
ops.doc:
A sequence's float curve names (containing `contains`).
Example: film-ue op anim.curves anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1 contains=eyeLook

ops.name: anim.describe
ops.summary: What an animation is: length, frames, rate, skeleton, its float curves (count, and which face groups),
ops.doc:
What an animation is: length, frames, rate, skeleton, its float curves (count, and which face groups),
bone tracks, additive settings, root motion, and the perf metadata (fingerprint) when perf made it.

Args: anim: AnimSequence path. curves: also list every curve name.
Returns: {"path", "length_s", "frames" (key intervals: keys - 1), "fps", "skeleton", "curve_count", "head_curves": [...],
"face_curves": n, "bone_tracks": n, "additive": {"type", "base"}, "root_motion": bool, "perf": {...}, "curves"?}.
Example: film-ue op anim.describe anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1

ops.name: anim.find
ops.summary: Search the project's animations (AnimSequence) by plain words, ranked: "happy face loop", "walk forward loop",
ops.doc:
Search the project's animations (AnimSequence) by plain words, ranked: "happy face loop", "walk forward loop",
"idle body". MetaHuman template names are understood (face/body, emotion, gait, start/loop/stop, direction).

Args: query: words (empty = everything under `path`). path: folder to search ("/" = all mounted content,
"/MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Animation" = the MetaHuman templates). skeleton: only animations on this skeleton
(a Skeleton, SkeletalMesh or AnimSequence path: "the face's skeleton" = the face mesh). kind: face|body.
min_s/max_s: length bounds in seconds (0 = none). limit: how many.
Returns: {"found": [{"path", "score", "kind", "category", "emotion", "gait", "phase", "direction", "tags",
"length_s", "skeleton"}], "total": n}.
Example: film-ue op anim.find query='walk forward loop' path=/MetaHumanCharacter

ops.name: anim.gaze_lock
ops.summary: Keep a talking face's eyes on the lens, measured rather than guessed: `out` (a copy of `anim`) goes on
ops.doc:
Keep a talking face's eyes on the lens, measured rather than guessed: `out` (a copy of `anim`) goes on
`component`'s track in `sequence` (on the sections that play `anim`, wherever they start); the eye-look curves are
calibrated on the rig, then solved per frame from the eye bones' real pose (head and body motion included)
toward `camera`, with small saccades, and refined `iterations` times against a fresh measurement.
`target` aims the eyes elsewhere: a point [x, y, z], an actor (+ `target_offset` in its frame) or
"Label:Component:bone" (her eyes: "Presenter:Face:FACIAL_L_Eye"); with `frames` [first, last] only in that range
(the camera, if given, elsewhere). Frames with neither keep the animation's own eye curves. Returns the angle error
per pass. A multi-tick job.
Example: film-ue op anim.gaze_lock sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 actor_label=Presenter anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1 out=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1_eyes camera=CAM_A

ops.name: anim.head_to_body
ops.summary: Give the body the head motion a face rig makes from speech (HeadYaw/Pitch/Roll spread down the neck): bake the
ops.doc:
Give the body the head motion a face rig makes from speech (HeadYaw/Pitch/Roll spread down the neck): bake the
face's spine, neck and head as they play into `out` (a copy of the body's animation), which goes on the body's
track. Then bake_follow puts the whole shared skeleton back on the face, so both move as one. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op anim.head_to_body sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 actor_label=Presenter body_anim=/Game/Anim/AS_idle out=/Game/Anim/AS_idle_head

ops.name: anim.new
ops.summary: An empty animation (no keys: the skeleton's reference pose) on a skeleton, `length_s` long at `fps`: a canvas
ops.doc:
An empty animation (no keys: the skeleton's reference pose) on a skeleton, `length_s` long at `fps`: a canvas
for perf.face, anim.write_curves or a procedural additive. Converges: an existing one of the same skeleton is
resized in place (its curves kept) unless `replace`.

Args: path: /Game/... package path. skeleton: a Skeleton, SkeletalMesh or AnimSequence whose skeleton to use.
length_s: seconds. fps: frame rate of the keys.
Returns: {"path", "changed", "created", "frames", "length_s"}.
Example: film-ue op anim.new path=/Game/Perf/AS_blank skeleton=/Game/MetaHumans/Ada/Face/Ada_FaceMesh length_s=5

ops.name: anim.read_curves
ops.summary: Float curves of an animation as {name: [times_s, values]}: all, the `names` given, or those whose name
ops.doc:
Float curves of an animation as {name: [times_s, values]}: all, the `names` given, or those whose name
contains `contains`; every n-th key. For client-side analysis (perfkit.metrics, plots).
Example: film-ue op anim.read_curves anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1 contains=Head

ops.name: anim.retarget
ops.summary: Retarget animations from one skeleton to another (a Mixamo or UE5 mannequin clip onto a MetaHuman body) by
ops.doc:
Retarget animations from one skeleton to another (a Mixamo or UE5 mannequin clip onto a MetaHuman body) by
code: IK Rigs for both meshes (auto-generated chains + full-body IK, made once under out_folder/Rigs unless
given), an IK Retargeter (default op stack, chains auto-mapped by name, the target's retarget pose auto-aligned
to the source), then the engine's batch retarget into `out_folder`, overwriting earlier results of the same name.

Args: anims: AnimSequence paths on the source skeleton. source_mesh/target_mesh: SkeletalMesh paths.
out_folder: /Game/... folder for the results and the rigs. source_rig/target_rig/retargeter: existing assets to
use instead of making them. suffix: added to each result's name. align: auto-align the target's retarget pose
(fixes T-pose vs A-pose). include_referenced: also retarget assets the inputs reference.
Returns: {"changed", "results": [paths], "retargeter", "rigs": {"source", "target"}, "made": [paths]}.
Example: film-ue op anim.retarget 'anims=["/Game/Mixamo/Wave"]' source_mesh=/Game/Mixamo/Y_Bot target_mesh=/Game/MetaHumans/Ada/Body/m_med_nrw_body out_folder=/Game/Anim/Retargeted

ops.name: anim.rig_controls
ops.summary: The controls of the Control Rig on an actor (or its component) in a sequence, for anim.rig_keys.
ops.doc:
The controls of the Control Rig on an actor (or its component) in a sequence, for anim.rig_keys.
Returns: {"rig": class name, "controls": [names]}.
Example: film-ue op anim.rig_controls sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 label=Presenter component=Face

ops.name: anim.rig_keys
ops.summary: Key Control Rig controls in a sequence, batched per control (one engine call each, not one per key).
ops.doc:
Key Control Rig controls in a sequence, batched per control (one engine call each, not one per key).
keys: {control: [[frame, value], ...]} where value is a number (a float control), {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} (a
rotator control) or {"loc": [x, y, z], "rot": {...}} (a transform control, local space). The rig track is found
on the actor (or `component`'s) binding, or made from `rig_class` (a Blueprint-based Control Rig asset path, or
a class path; 5.8's independent Control Rig assets cannot be made into a track from Python; `layered` for an
additive layer over the animation).
Returns: {"changed", "controls": n, "keys": n, "rig"}.
Example: film-ue op anim.rig_keys sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 label=Presenter component=Face 'keys={"CTRL_L_brow_raiseIn": [[0,0],[12,0.6],[30,0]]}'

ops.name: anim.scale_curves
ops.summary: Multiply (then offset) curves by name: {"HeadYaw": 0.6, "CTRL_expressions_browRaiseInL": 1.3}. Not idempotent:
ops.doc:
Multiply (then offset) curves by name: {"HeadYaw": 0.6, "CTRL_expressions_browRaiseInL": 1.3}. Not idempotent:
each call scales again.
Example: film-ue op anim.scale_curves anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1 'scale={"HeadYaw": 0.6}'

ops.name: anim.set_curve
ops.summary: Replace a curve with these keys (times in seconds). anim.write_curves writes many in one batch.
ops.doc:
Replace a curve with these keys (times in seconds). anim.write_curves writes many in one batch.
Example: film-ue op anim.set_curve anim=/Game/Perf/AS_face name=CTRL_expressions_browRaiseInL 'times=[0,1,2]' 'values=[0,0.5,0]'

ops.name: anim.write_curves
ops.summary: Write many float curves in one batch (one controller bracket, one recompression): {name: [times_s, values]}.
ops.doc:
Write many float curves in one batch (one controller bracket, one recompression): {name: [times_s, values]}.
mode: "replace" (these keys only), "add" (added to the curve's current values), "max", "mul".

Returns: {"anim", "changed", "curves": n, "keys": total}.
Example: film-ue op anim.write_curves anim=/Game/Perf/AS_face 'curves={"CTRL_expressions_browRaiseInL": [[0,1,2],[0,0.4,0]]}'

ops.name: assets.audit
ops.summary: What in a folder needs attention: assets nothing uses (and no level), redirectors, materials that do not
ops.doc:
What in a folder needs attention: assets nothing uses (and no level), redirectors, materials that do not
compile (they draw the engine's checker), material instances whose textures do not match their samplers.

Args: folder: content folder (recursive). unused: report unused assets. broken: compile-check materials (loads
      them: slower). limit: at most this many of each.
Returns: {"pass", "issues": [{"code": asset.unused | asset.redirector | material.not_compiling |
         material.texture_kind, "severity", "subject", "message", "fix"}], "metrics": {"assets", "unused",
         "redirectors", "broken"}}.
Example: film-ue op assets.audit folder=/Game/Props

ops.name: assets.catalog
ops.summary: The assets of a folder as data, from the asset registry (no loading): path, class, size in cm, triangles,
ops.doc:
The assets of a folder as data, from the asset registry (no loading): path, class, size in cm, triangles,
LODs, Nanite, material count, texture size/format, source file. Cached in Saved/fmbridge/catalog.json.

Args: folder: content folder (recursive). cls: one class (StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh, Texture2D, Material,
      MaterialInstanceConstant, Blueprint, SoundWave, AnimSequence, GroomAsset, ...). refresh: rebuild now.
      load: also load meshes whose counts are missing, and read metadata tags (slower). max_age_s: reuse a
      cached catalog this young. limit: at most this many entries returned.
Returns: {"folder", "count", "built_at", "entries": [{"path", "name", "class", "size_cm": [x, y, z],
         "triangles", "lods", "nanite", "materials", "dimensions", "format", "source", "tags"}]}.
Example: film-ue op assets.catalog folder=/Game/Props cls=StaticMesh

ops.name: assets.delete
ops.summary: Delete an asset now, used or not (prefer assets.remove, which checks who uses it first); False if absent.
ops.doc:
Delete an asset now, used or not (prefer assets.remove, which checks who uses it first); False if absent.
Example: film-ue assets delete --path /Game/Old/SM_Box

ops.name: assets.describe
ops.summary: One asset as numbers: class, size in cm and bounds, triangles/vertices per LOD, Nanite, collision, material
ops.doc:
One asset as numbers: class, size in cm and bounds, triangles/vertices per LOD, Nanite, collision, material
slots (meshes); size, sRGB, compression, LOD group (textures); parent and parameters (materials: see
mat.describe); skeleton, bones (skeletal); duration (sounds); source file; metadata tags; who uses it.

Args: path: /Game/... asset. refs: include referencers/dependencies.
Returns: {"path", "class", ...per class..., "source", "tags", "referencers", "dependencies"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.describe path=/Game/Props/SM_Chair

ops.name: assets.duplicate
ops.summary: Copy an asset (a MetaHuman preset, a material...) to a new path; an existing `dst` is kept unless overwrite
ops.doc:
Copy an asset (a MetaHuman preset, a material...) to a new path; an existing `dst` is kept unless overwrite
(then it is freed first). Returns dst.
Example: film-ue assets duplicate --src /Game/M/MI_A --dst /Game/M/MI_B

ops.name: assets.find
ops.summary: Search assets by what they are and how big: words (name, folders, tags; a few synonyms: sofa/couch...), a
ops.doc:
Search assets by what they are and how big: words (name, folders, tags; a few synonyms: sofa/couch...), a
size ("a 45 cm chair", "table 120x80 cm", "lamp 1.5 m tall"), class, a name glob, tags, size bounds. Each hit
says how far its size is from the asked one and the uniform scale that would make it exact.

Args: query: plain words with optional sizes (mm/cm/m/in/ft; no unit = cm; tall/wide/long pick the axis).
      cls: StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh, Texture2D, MaterialInstanceConstant, ... folder: where to look.
      name: a glob on the asset name (SM_Chair*). tags: {key: value} metadata tags (assets.tag) to match.
      min_size_cm / max_size_cm: [x, y, z] bounds the size must be within (0 = no bound on that axis).
      limit: at most this many. refresh: rebuild the catalog first.
Returns: {"query": parsed, "hits": [{"path", "class", "size_cm", "score" 0..1, "size_error", "scale", ...}],
         "count"}. Nothing found: hits [] and a hint.
Example: film-ue op assets.find 'query=a 45 cm chair' cls=StaticMesh

ops.name: assets.fix_redirectors
ops.summary: Repoint everything that references a redirector (left behind by a rename/move) at the real asset and delete
ops.doc:
Repoint everything that references a redirector (left behind by a rename/move) at the real asset and delete
the redirectors, without a dialog.

Args: folder: where to look (recursive).
Returns: {"fixed": int, "left": [redirectors that could not be fixed], "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.fix_redirectors folder=/Game/Props

ops.name: assets.folder
ops.summary: Content folders: make one, rename/move one (with everything in it), or remove an empty one.
ops.doc:
Content folders: make one, rename/move one (with everything in it), or remove an empty one.

Args: path: /Game/... folder. action: make | rename | remove. to: the new folder path for rename.
Returns: {"path", "changed", "to"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.folder path=/Game/Props/Chairs

ops.name: assets.import
ops.summary: Import files on the box into a content folder, any format, with no dialog: FBX/OBJ/glTF/GLB (Interchange),
ops.doc:
Import files on the box into a content folder, any format, with no dialog: FBX/OBJ/glTF/GLB (Interchange),
Alembic (static, geometry cache, skeletal, or a groom), USD, images (settings by role, see
assets.import_textures), WAV. Returns the new assets' object paths (or with detail, per file).

Args: files: paths on the box. dest: content folder. replace: re-import over existing (an Interchange re-import);
      false keeps what an earlier import of the same file made in dest (changed false).
      combine: merge an FBX's parts into one static mesh. kind: static | skeletal | auto (what the file says) |
      geometry_cache (Alembic). skeleton: /Game/... Skeleton for skeletal meshes/animations (else a new one).
      scale: uniform import scale (the source's units are converted to cm first). nanite: build Nanite (default
      on for static). collision: none | box | sphere | capsule | convex | convex10 | convex26 (a simple shape
      generated). lods: import LODs in the file. materials/textures: import the file's materials and textures.
      animations: import animations. groom: an Alembic of hair curves -> a Groom asset. abc_preset: maya | max |
      none (Alembic axis conversion). name: asset name for a single file. detail: return
      {"imported": [{"file", "kind", "assets", "objects"}], "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.import 'files=["/data/props/chair.fbx"]' dest=/Game/Props/Chair collision=convex

ops.name: assets.import_textures
ops.summary: Import image files as textures with the right settings for what each is: the role from its name
ops.doc:
Import image files as textures with the right settings for what each is: the role from its name
(T_Rock_BaseColor, _Normal, _ORM, _Roughness, _AO, ... see assets.md), a PNG named nothing useful but that looks
like a normal map is one, else colour.

Args: files: images on the box. folder: every image in a box folder. dest: content folder. role: force one
      role for all. replace: import again over existing textures (else kept).
Returns: {"textures": [{"file", "path", "role", "imported"}], "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.import_textures folder=/data/tex/rock dest=/Game/Rock/Textures

ops.name: assets.list
ops.summary: Assets under a path, optionally of one class name ('StaticMesh', 'MetaHumanCharacter', ...): [class, path].
ops.doc:
Assets under a path, optionally of one class name ('StaticMesh', 'MetaHumanCharacter', ...): [class, path].
(For search by name, size, tags use assets.find; for one asset's numbers assets.describe.)
Example: film-ue assets list --path /Game/Props --cls StaticMesh

ops.name: assets.mesh
ops.summary: Converge a static mesh's build settings: Nanite, generated LODs, simple collision, lightmap UVs, CPU access.
ops.doc:
Converge a static mesh's build settings: Nanite, generated LODs, simple collision, lightmap UVs, CPU access.

Args: path: /Game/... StaticMesh. nanite: on/off. nanite_keep_percent: 0..100 triangles kept by Nanite.
      lods: number of LODs to generate (1 = just the base; generated by reduction: LOD i keeps lod_percents[i] %
      of the triangles, default 100, 50, 25, 12.5...). collision: none (remove simple collision) | box | sphere |
      capsule | convex (a decomposition into convex_hulls hulls) | ndop10 | ndop18 | ndop26. lightmap_uv:
      generate lightmap UVs. cpu_access: allow CPU access (needed to read vertices at runtime).
      lod_group: a LOD group name (LargeProp, SmallProp, HighDetail, ...).
Returns: {"path", "changed", "set": [...], "lods", "triangles", "nanite", "collision_prims"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.mesh path=/Game/Props/SM_Chair nanite=true collision=convex convex_hulls=8

ops.name: assets.move
ops.summary: Move assets into a folder, keeping their names (references follow).
ops.doc:
Move assets into a folder, keeping their names (references follow).

Args: paths: /Game/... assets. folder: destination folder. fix_redirectors: as assets.rename.
Returns: {"moved": {src: dst}, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.move 'paths=["/Game/Imports/SM_Chair"]' folder=/Game/Props

ops.name: assets.props
ops.summary: An asset's editor properties (all readable ones, or the named), as text.
ops.doc:
An asset's editor properties (all readable ones, or the named), as text.
Example: film-ue assets props --path /Game/T/T_Wood_D --names srgb,compression_settings

ops.name: assets.refs
ops.summary: Who uses an asset (referencers) and what it uses (dependencies), from the asset registry; with depth > 1 the
ops.doc:
Who uses an asset (referencers) and what it uses (dependencies), from the asset registry; with depth > 1 the
tree is followed that many levels.

Args: path: /Game/... asset. depth: levels to follow (1 = direct only, max 5).
Returns: {"path", "referencers": [paths], "dependencies": [paths], "level_actors": [labels using it in the open
         level], "tree": {path: {"referencers", "dependencies"}} when depth > 1}.
Example: film-ue op assets.refs path=/Game/Mats/MI_Oak

ops.name: assets.reimport
ops.summary: Re-import an asset from its source file (or from a new file), keeping its settings, with no dialog.
ops.doc:
Re-import an asset from its source file (or from a new file), keeping its settings, with no dialog.

Args: path: /Game/... asset. file: a new source file on the box (else the one it was imported from).
Returns: {"path", "source", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.reimport path=/Game/Props/SM_Chair file=/data/props/chair_v2.fbx

ops.name: assets.remove
ops.summary: Delete assets safely: refused (code conflict, naming who) while another asset or the open level uses them,
ops.doc:
Delete assets safely: refused (code conflict, naming who) while another asset or the open level uses them,
unless force. Removing what is not there is fine.

Args: paths: /Game/... assets. folder: every asset under a content folder (and the folder). force: delete even
      if referenced (referencers then point at nothing: they render the default material/mesh). dry_run: only
      report what would go (removed) and what is in use (kept).
Returns: {"removed": [paths], "kept": {path: [referencers]}, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.remove 'paths=["/Game/Old/SM_Box"]'

ops.name: assets.rename
ops.summary: Rename or move an asset (references follow), without a dialog; re-running after it moved changes nothing.
ops.doc:
Rename or move an asset (references follow), without a dialog; re-running after it moved changes nothing.

Args: src: current /Game/... path. dst: new path (another folder moves it). fix_redirectors: repoint every
      referencer at the new path and delete the redirector left at src.
Returns: {"src", "dst", "changed", "redirectors_fixed": int}.
Example: film-ue op assets.rename src=/Game/Imports/chair dst=/Game/Props/Chairs/SM_Chair

ops.name: assets.save
ops.summary: Save assets by path, or every dirty asset under a folder.
ops.doc:
Save assets by path, or every dirty asset under a folder.

Args: paths: /Game/... assets. folder: a content folder (recursive).
Returns: {"saved": [paths], "failed": [paths], "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.save folder=/Game/Props

ops.name: assets.save_all
ops.summary: Save every dirty package and map.
ops.doc:
Save every dirty package and map.
Example: film-ue assets save_all

ops.name: assets.set_props
ops.summary: Set editor properties on an asset (enums by name, e.g. {"lod_group": "TEXTUREGROUP_WORLD"}).
ops.doc:
Set editor properties on an asset (enums by name, e.g. {"lod_group": "TEXTUREGROUP_WORLD"}).

Args: path: /Game/... asset. props: {property: value}; an enum value is "ENUM_NAME" or "EnumClass.ENUM_NAME".
      save: save the asset.
Returns: {"path", "changed", "set": [names]}.
Example: film-ue op assets.set_props path=/Game/T/T_Wood_D 'props={"max_texture_size": 2048}'

ops.name: assets.tag
ops.summary: Metadata tags on an asset (searchable by assets.find tags=...): set or remove key/values.
ops.doc:
Metadata tags on an asset (searchable by assets.find tags=...): set or remove key/values.

Args: path: /Game/... asset. set: {key: value} strings. remove: keys to drop.
Returns: {"path", "tags": {key: value}, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.tag path=/Game/Props/SM_Chair 'set={"category": "furniture", "style": "mid-century"}'

ops.name: assets.texture
ops.summary: Converge a texture's settings: by role (base_color/emissive/translucency: sRGB colour; normal: TC_NORMALMAP
ops.doc:
Converge a texture's settings: by role (base_color/emissive/translucency: sRGB colour; normal: TC_NORMALMAP
linear; roughness/metallic/ao/orm/opacity/height/specular: TC_MASKS linear; hdr) and/or explicit ones.

Args: path: /Game/... texture. role: a role (see above). srgb: override. compression: TC_DEFAULT, TC_NORMALMAP,
      TC_MASKS, TC_GRAYSCALE, TC_HDR, TC_BC7, ... max_size_px: cap (0 = none). flip_green: OpenGL normal maps.
      lod_group: TEXTUREGROUP_WORLD, TEXTUREGROUP_CHARACTER, ... virtual_texture: virtual texture streaming.
      mips: TMGS_FROM_TEXTURE_GROUP, TMGS_NO_MIPMAPS, ...
Returns: {"path", "changed", "set": [settings written]}.
Example: film-ue op assets.texture path=/Game/T/T_Rock_N role=normal

ops.name: assets.thumbnail
ops.summary: Pictures of an asset with no viewport: a temporary actor of it is placed away from the set, captured alone
ops.doc:
Pictures of an asset with no viewport: a temporary actor of it is placed away from the set, captured alone
(WP10's view.turntable with isolate), and removed. One view (a 3/4 shot) or several around it plus a sheet.
The open level's lights reach it only if it is placed among them (loc); `light` adds a temporary point light
above and in front of it, removed afterwards.

Args: path: /Game/... StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh or Blueprint. out_dir: where the PNGs go on the box. views: how
      many. size_px: square size. elevation_deg/yaw_deg: the camera's angle above and around it. loc: where the
      temporary actor stands [x, y, z] cm (default far below the set). light: add a temporary key light.
Returns: {"path", "views": [{"yaw", "path"}], "sheet", "size_cm"}. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op assets.thumbnail path=/Game/Props/SM_Chair out_dir=/tmp/thumbs/chair views=4

ops.name: audio.describe
ops.summary: A sequence's audio tracks and clips, with frames and seconds.
ops.doc:
A sequence's audio tracks and clips, with frames and seconds.

Args: sequence: the LevelSequence path.
Returns: {"sequence", "fps", "tracks": [{"name", "clips": [{"sound", "start_frame", "end_frame", "row",
"offset_s", "volume_db", "fade_in_frames", "fade_out_frames", "start_s", "end_s"}]}]}.
Example: film-ue op audio.describe sequence=/Game/Seq/SQ_Main

ops.name: audio.import
ops.summary: Import WAV files on the box as SoundWaves in `folder`, skipping any already there (idempotent).
ops.doc:
Import WAV files on the box as SoundWaves in `folder`, skipping any already there (idempotent).

Args: files: absolute WAV paths on the box (push them first: client.push). folder: content folder. names:
{file: asset name} to override the default (the file's stem, sanitised). replace: re-import over an existing
sound (its source changed). save: save the new assets.
Returns: {"changed", "sounds": [{"file", "path", "duration_s", "imported"}]}.
Example: film-ue op audio.import 'files=["/srv/film/vo/L1.wav"]' folder=/Game/Audio/VO

ops.name: audio.lines
ops.summary: Import a timing document's voice lines and place each at its frame on one track: the voice, timed, in one call.
ops.doc:
Import a timing document's voice lines and place each at its frame on one track: the voice, timed, in one call.

Args: sequence: LevelSequence path. timing: a timing document (filmtools.unreal.audio_timing:
{"kind": "timing", "fps", "lines": [{"id", "wav", "start_frame", ...}]}). folder: where the SoundWaves go.
track: the track's name. wav_root: a box directory the lines' relative `wav` paths are under. extend: lengthen
the playback range to the last line. replace: the track holds exactly these lines (False: they are added to
what is there, a line already at its frame left alone; for adding one line at a time).
Returns: {"changed", "lines": [{"id", "sound", "start_frame", "end_frame"}], "fps_note"?}.
Example: film-ue op audio.lines sequence=/Game/Seq/SQ_Main wav_root=/srv/film/vo timing=@timing.json

ops.name: audio.place
ops.summary: Put sounds on a named audio track of a sequence at their frames; re-running with the same clips changes nothing.
ops.doc:
Put sounds on a named audio track of a sequence at their frames; re-running with the same clips changes nothing.

Args: sequence: LevelSequence path. clips: [{"sound": SoundWave path, "start_frame" (or "start_s"),
"end_frame" or "duration_s" (default: to the sound's end), "offset_s" (seconds into the sound, default 0),
"volume_db" (default 0), "fade_in_frames"/"fade_out_frames" (linear ramps from/to silence), "id"?}] or [sound, start_frame] pairs. track: the track's name ("VO", "Music", "SFX").
replace: the track holds exactly these clips (else they are added to it; one already there at the same frame
is left as it is). extend: lengthen the playback range
to the last clip's end.
Returns: {"changed", "track", "clips": [{"sound", "start_frame", "end_frame", "row", "offset_s", "volume_db"}],
"end_frame"}.
Example: film-ue op audio.place sequence=/Game/Seq/SQ_Main track=VO 'clips=[{"sound":"/Game/Audio/VO/L1","start_frame":48}]'

ops.name: audio.remove
ops.summary: Remove a named audio track from a sequence (nothing to remove is fine).
ops.doc:
Remove a named audio track from a sequence (nothing to remove is fine).

Args: sequence: LevelSequence path. track: the track's name, or "*" for every audio track.
Returns: {"changed", "removed": [names]}.
Example: film-ue op audio.remove sequence=/Game/Seq/SQ_Main track=VO

ops.name: bridge.health
ops.summary: The bridge's state: engine, platform, project, uptime, protocol version, jobs, memory, idle cap, seconds
ops.doc:
The bridge's state: engine, platform, project, uptime, protocol version, jobs, memory, idle cap, seconds
since the last tick (a large value means the game thread is stuck).

Returns: the /health dict: {"ok", "engine", "platform", "project", "uptime", "bridge", "python", "pid", "rss_mb",
"jobs", "idle_fps", "throttle_off", "last_tick_s", "idle_s"}.
Example: film-ue op bridge.health

ops.name: cam.add
ops.summary: Make or converge a cine camera named `label`: place it, aim it, set its lens and focus.
ops.doc:
Make or converge a cine camera named `label`: place it, aim it, set its lens and focus.

Args: label: actor label. loc: [x, y, z] cm. rot_: {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} deg, or look_at: a point [x, y, z],
an actor label or "Label:Component:bone" (overrides rot_). focal_mm. aperture: f-stop. sensor_mm: [w, h] mm, or
filmback: a preset name ("16:9 Digital Film", the engine default; "16:9 DSLR" is full frame). lens_preset:
"50mm Prime f/1.8" etc. (sets the lens limits). focus_cm: manual focus distance; focus_on: a point/actor/bone
to focus on now (manual focus at its distance; for a moving subject key it with cam.move focus_on, or use
cam.focus mode=track).
A new camera gets the engine's default filmback and focal 35 mm unless given.
Returns: cam.describe's dict plus "changed", "created".
Example: film-ue op cam.add label=CAM_A 'loc=[400,0,160]' look_at=Presenter focal_mm=50 aperture=2.8

ops.name: cam.check
ops.summary: Numeric checks of a camera's frame on its subjects: QA's per-frame framing (headroom, cut-offs, feet, size, look
ops.doc:
Numeric checks of a camera's frame on its subjects: QA's per-frame framing (headroom, cut-offs, feet, size, look
room; when fmbridge.qa is installed) plus the camera's own: focus, safe areas, an accidental dutch, a subject
blocked by `others`.

Returns: {"pass", "issues": [{"code", "severity", "message", "fix", ...}], "metrics": {"size", "focus_cm",
"hfov_deg"}}.
Example: film-ue op cam.check camera=CAM_A subjects=Presenter size=MCU

ops.name: cam.check_cut
ops.summary: Would a cut from camera A to camera B work: the 180-degree line between the first two subjects, the
ops.doc:
Would a cut from camera A to camera B work: the 180-degree line between the first two subjects, the
30-degree rule and the size step on the first.

Example: film-ue op cam.check_cut camera_a=CAM_A camera_b=CAM_B 'subjects=["Host","Guest"]'

ops.name: cam.coverage
ops.summary: The coverage of a scene, all on one side of the line: for one subject a WS/MS/MCU/CU from 3/4 and a profile;
ops.doc:
The coverage of a scene, all on one side of the line: for one subject a WS/MS/MCU/CU from 3/4 and a profile;
for two or more a master, a two-shot, each one's MS/MCU/CU single and an over-the-shoulder. Makes a camera per
shot ({prefix}{name}) unless create=False.

Args: side: left|right of the line from the first subject to the second, seen from above.
Returns: {"line", "side", "shots": [{"name", "camera", "kind", "size", "focal", "distance", "loc", "rot",
"warnings"}], "issues"}.
Example: film-ue op cam.coverage 'subjects=["Host","Guest"]' side=left

ops.name: cam.describe
ops.summary: Every cine camera in the level (or one): location, rotation, focal, aperture, filmback, focus, fields of view,
ops.doc:
Every cine camera in the level (or one): location, rotation, focal, aperture, filmback, focus, fields of view,
the rig it hangs on; with `subjects`, also each camera's shot in words ("MCU of Host from 3/4 left (41 deg), eye
level, 50 mm f/2.8, right third"), which cam.shoot reads back.

Example: film-ue op cam.describe label=CAM_A subjects=Host

ops.name: cam.focus
ops.summary: Set a camera's focus: mode "manual" (distance_cm, or the distance to `target` now), "track" (follow an actor,
ops.doc:
Set a camera's focus: mode "manual" (distance_cm, or the distance to `target` now), "track" (follow an actor,
the engine's tracking focus: `target` an actor label, or "eyes:Label" for its eyes at the current pose, or
"Label:Component:bone"), or "off" (no depth of field).

Args: offset: cm in the tracked actor's own frame, added to the target. smooth_speed: >0 smooths focus changes.
Example: film-ue op cam.focus label=CAM_A mode=track target=eyes:Presenter

ops.name: cam.frame
ops.summary: Frame subjects with a camera by shot grammar: "MCU of Presenter from 3/4 left, eye level, 50 mm".
ops.doc:
Frame subjects with a camera by shot grammar: "MCU of Presenter from 3/4 left, eye level, 50 mm".

Args: camera: label (made if missing). subjects: an actor label or a list (a two-shot, a group).
size: ECU CU MCU MS COWBOY MWS WS EWS (aliases: close-up, medium, wide, full...). angle: degrees or front, 3/4,
profile, 3/4 back, back: around from the first subject's facing toward its own `side` (left|right).
height: eye, high, low, slight high, slight low, overhead, worm, degrees, shoulder/chest/hip/knee/ground, or
{"z": cm}. focal_mm (distance solved) or distance_cm with focal_mm=None (focal solved; snap_focal rounds to a
prime). place: auto (thirds with lead room off-axis, centre when frontal), center, left third, right third, or
u 0..1. headroom: v of the head's top (default per size). dutch_deg: roll. focus: focus on the first subject's
eyes. apply: False only plans (nothing changes).
Returns: {"camera": cam.describe dict, "solve": {distance, focal, error, predicted u/v of every landmark,
dof, warnings}, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op cam.frame camera=CAM_A subjects=Presenter size=MCU angle=3/4 side=left focal_mm=50

ops.name: cam.move
ops.summary: Key camera moves into a sequence: dolly, push_in, pull_out, truck, pedestal, crane, orbit/arc, pan, tilt,
ops.doc:
Key camera moves into a sequence: dolly, push_in, pull_out, truck, pedestal, crane, orbit/arc, pan, tilt,
roll, zoom, dolly_zoom, whip, rack, follow, hold; eased, one after another from the camera's current pose, with
optional handheld noise. Replaces the camera's transform (and focal/focus) tracks in that sequence.

Args: moves_: [{"move": kind, "frames": n | "from"/"to", "ease": in_out|in|out|linear|sine|smooth|expo, ...}]
(cam.presets lists kinds; docs/unreal/camera.md their arguments). aim: what the camera keeps framed (a point, an
actor label, "Label:Component:bone", "eyes:Label"). focus_on: the same, baked as a follow-focus. noise: "subtle"
| "handheld" | "documentary" | "breathing" | "shake" or {"preset", "seed", "scale", "pos", "rot", "hz"}.
step: frames between baked keys. end_frame: hold the last pose to there.
A multi-tick job (the keys go in one batched seq.apply when WP8's core is there).
Returns: {"keys": {"transform", "focal", "focus"}, "segments", "first", "last", "write", "changed": true}.
Example: film-ue op cam.move camera=CAM_A sequence=/Game/Seq/S1 'moves_=[{"move":"push_in","fraction":0.2,"frames":72}]' aim=eyes:Presenter

ops.name: cam.point
ops.summary: Where a target is now, in world cm: a point, an actor label (its location; with `offset` in its own frame),
ops.doc:
Where a target is now, in world cm: a point, an actor label (its location; with `offset` in its own frame),
"Label:Component:bone", "eyes:Label" (between its eyes), or a camera's label (its lens).

Example: film-ue op cam.point target=eyes:Presenter

ops.name: cam.presets
ops.summary: The filmback and lens presets (the engine's own, from BaseEngine.ini) and the shot sizes, angles and heights
ops.doc:
The filmback and lens presets (the engine's own, from BaseEngine.ini) and the shot sizes, angles and heights
the framing solver knows.

Returns: {"filmbacks": {name: [w_mm, h_mm]}, "lenses": {name: {...}}, "default_filmback", "sizes": {key: desc},
"angles", "heights", "moves", "noise"}.
Example: film-ue op cam.presets

ops.name: cam.project
ops.summary: Where things land in a camera's frame: u, v (0..1 from the top left; outside = out of frame) and depth (cm),
ops.doc:
Where things land in a camera's frame: u, v (0..1 from the top left; outside = out of frame) and depth (cm),
for named points ({"name": [x, y, z] | label | "Label:Component:bone"}) and every landmark of `subjects`.

Example: film-ue op cam.project camera=CAM_A subjects=Presenter

ops.name: cam.remove
ops.summary: Delete cine cameras (and rigs) by label or by label prefix; missing ones are skipped.
ops.doc:
Delete cine cameras (and rigs) by label or by label prefix; missing ones are skipped.

Example: film-ue op cam.remove prefix=CAM_

ops.name: cam.rig
ops.summary: A camera rail or crane (the engine's CameraRig_Rail / CameraRig_Crane), with `camera` mounted on it.
ops.doc:
A camera rail or crane (the engine's CameraRig_Rail / CameraRig_Crane), with `camera` mounted on it.

rail: `points` [[x, y, z], ...] world cm along the track (2+); `position` 0..1 along it; lock_orientation turns
the camera with the rail. crane: at `loc`, turned `yaw_deg`, arm `arm_cm` long, raised `pitch_deg`. Drive either
over time with cam.rig_move.
Example: film-ue op cam.rig label=Rail_A kind=rail 'points=[[300,-200,150],[300,200,150]]' camera=CAM_A

ops.name: cam.rig_move
ops.summary: Animate a rig in a sequence: a rail's position along it (0..1), a crane's pitch, yaw and arm.
ops.doc:
Animate a rig in a sequence: a rail's position along it (0..1), a crane's pitch, yaw and arm.

Args: keys: [[frame, {"position": 0..1} | {"pitch_deg", "yaw_deg", "arm_cm"}], ...] (auto-eased).
Example: film-ue op cam.rig_move rig_label=Rail_A sequence=/Game/Seq/S1 'keys=[[0,{"position":0}],[96,{"position":1}]]'

ops.name: cam.set
ops.summary: Change an existing camera's lens: focal length (or the horizontal field of view it gives), aperture,
ops.doc:
Change an existing camera's lens: focal length (or the horizontal field of view it gives), aperture,
filmback, lens limits, near clip plane.

Example: film-ue op cam.set label=CAM_A focal_mm=85 aperture=1.8

ops.name: cam.shoot
ops.summary: Frame a camera from a sentence of shot grammar: "medium close-up of Host from 30 deg left at eye level, 50mm",
ops.doc:
Frame a camera from a sentence of shot grammar: "medium close-up of Host from 30 deg left at eye level, 50mm",
"two-shot of Host and Guest, low angle, 35mm", "CU of Guest from 3/4 right, 2 m away" (the focal length solved).
The subjects are the level's actor labels found in the text. Words it does not understand are returned in
`unparsed` (nothing is guessed); the vocabulary is in docs/unreal/camera.md.

Returns: cam.frame's result plus {"parsed": the arguments it read, "words": the camera described back}.
Example: film-ue op cam.shoot camera=CAM_A text='MCU of Host from 3/4 left, eye level, 50mm'

ops.name: cam.still
ops.summary: A still through a camera with the operator's guides drawn on it: thirds, action/title safe, centre, and each
ops.doc:
A still through a camera with the operator's guides drawn on it: thirds, action/title safe, centre, and each
subject's landmarks where the lens math puts them (green crosses), so a mismatch between solver and render shows.
A multi-tick job. Keep it small (960x540): the overlay is drawn in pure Python.

Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "raw": the still without guides}.
Example: film-ue op cam.still camera=CAM_A out=/tmp/cam_a.png subjects=Presenter

ops.name: cam.subject
ops.summary: What the framing solver sees of an actor: its landmarks (head_top, eyes, nose, mouth, chin, neck, shoulders,
ops.doc:
What the framing solver sees of an actor: its landmarks (head_top, eyes, nose, mouth, chin, neck, shoulders,
chest, waist, hips, knees, ankles, feet) in world cm, its facing and height, and whether they came from its
skeleton or its bounds.

Args: target: actor label. mode: auto (bones, else bounds) | bones | bounds. facing: [x, y, z] override.
top_z: the crown's height when hair or a hat makes it higher than the default (eyes + 11.5 cm).
Example: film-ue op cam.subject target=Presenter

ops.name: editor.api_names
ops.summary: Is every `unreal.<Name>` the bridge's code uses really in this editor's `unreal` module? The fake engine accepts
ops.doc:
Is every `unreal.<Name>` the bridge's code uses really in this editor's `unreal` module? The fake engine accepts
any name, so a C++ class name where Python wants the ScriptName (AutomationBlueprintFunctionLibrary vs
AutomationLibrary) or a plugin that is off only shows up here, or when the op runs.

Scans the installed fmbridge sources for `unreal.X` (the first name after `unreal.`), checks each with hasattr.
Returns: {"checked": int, "missing": {name: [files]}, "names": [all names] (only_missing=false)}.
A missing name is a bug (wrong name) or a disabled plugin: API_NOTES in docs/unreal/<area>.md says which.
Example: film-ue op editor.api_names

ops.name: editor.console
ops.summary: Run one console command in the editor (stat, r.*, Fab.Login, ...). It cannot report the command's own output:
ops.doc:
Run one console command in the editor (stat, r.*, Fab.Login, ...). It cannot report the command's own output:
read the log (film-ue log) or a cvar after it. Never run Fab.Logout or Fab.SetEnvironment: both delete the
saved Epic sign-in.

Args: command: the command line as typed in the console.
Returns: {"command", "ran": true}.
Example: film-ue op editor.console 'command=stat unit'

ops.name: editor.cvar
ops.summary: Read a console variable, or set it (through the console, as typed there) and read it back.
ops.doc:
Read a console variable, or set it (through the console, as typed there) and read it back.

Args: name: e.g. "r.RayTracing". value: the new value (number, bool or string); omit to only read.
Returns: {"name", "value": the value now (string), "before", "changed": bool}.
Example: film-ue op editor.cvar name=t.MaxFPS value=30

ops.name: editor.cvars
ops.summary: Console variables as a set: read several, set several, and take or restore a named snapshot (so a test or a
ops.doc:
Console variables as a set: read several, set several, and take or restore a named snapshot (so a test or a
render can change cvars and put them back). Snapshots live until the editor stops, and in Saved/Bridge/cvars.

Args: names: cvars to read. values: {name: value} to set (read back after). snapshot: save the current values of
`names` and of the keys of `values` under this name, before setting anything. restore: set the cvars of this
snapshot back.
Returns: {"values": {name: value now}, "changed": [names], "snapshot"?, "restored"?}.
Example: film-ue op editor.cvars 'values={"r.RayTracing": 0}' snapshot=pre

ops.name: editor.describe
ops.summary: What the editor is and how it is doing: engine, platform, RHI, project, open level, unsaved packages, idle cap,
ops.doc:
What the editor is and how it is doing: engine, platform, RHI, project, open level, unsaved packages, idle cap,
shader workers, memory, bridge jobs.

Returns: {"engine", "platform", "python", "rhi", "project", "level", "dirty": {"maps", "content"},
"idle_fps", "max_fps", "shader_workers", "rss_mb", "jobs": {"queued", "running"}, "uptime_s"}.
Example: film-ue op editor.describe

ops.name: editor.doctor
ops.summary: Check that this editor can do the work: engine 5.8, Python 3.11, a real GPU RHI (not -nullrhi), the plugins
ops.doc:
Check that this editor can do the work: engine 5.8, Python 3.11, a real GPU RHI (not -nullrhi), the plugins
the ops need, every op module imported, free disk, the Epic sign-in (Linux), the render/MetaHuman/data layer
APIs reachable from Python, and the hair sky-lighting trap. Read-only.

Returns: {"pass": no fail-severity issue, "issues": [{"code", "severity", "message", "fix"}], "metrics":
{"engine", "python", "platform", "rhi", "offscreen", "free_gb", "plugins_missing", "ops", "broken"}}.
Example: film-ue doctor   (or: film-ue op editor.doctor)

ops.name: editor.epic_exchange_code
ops.summary: Hand the MetaHuman cloud services a single-use Epic exchange code (MetaHuman.Cloud.Config.ExchangeCode), so
ops.doc:
Hand the MetaHuman cloud services a single-use Epic exchange code (MetaHuman.Cloud.Config.ExchangeCode), so
its next login (mh.rig, mh.textures) signs in without a browser and saves a sign-in for later starts
(MetaHumanCloudAuthentication.cpp: exchange code before persistent auth). The code itself is never returned or
kept by the bridge; the console echoes it to the editor log, where it is spent after use (~5 min validity).
Clients: film-ue epic-login --exchange-code-cmd CMD.

Args: code: the exchange code (from Epic's OAuth exchange endpoint; see docs/unreal/platform.md).
Returns: {"set": true}.
Example: film-ue epic-login --exchange-code-cmd ./my-exchange-code-helper

ops.name: editor.gc
ops.summary: Collect garbage (frees unreferenced objects after big imports or level changes) and report memory.
ops.doc:
Collect garbage (frees unreferenced objects after big imports or level changes) and report memory.

Returns: {"rss_mb_before", "rss_mb_after"} (Linux; None elsewhere).
Example: film-ue op editor.gc

ops.name: editor.idle
ops.summary: Cap an offscreen editor between jobs so it does not hold the GPU at full load: the frame rate (t.MaxFPS) and
ops.doc:
Cap an offscreen editor between jobs so it does not hold the GPU at full load: the frame rate (t.MaxFPS) and
whether the level viewport redraws every frame. Movie Render Queue lifts the cap while it renders (render.mrq).

Args: fps: the cap (0 = none). realtime: the level viewport in realtime.
Returns: {"fps", "realtime", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op editor.idle fps=10

ops.name: editor.plugins
ops.summary: The plugins: which are enabled now, and what the .uproject lists. With `enable`/`disable`, edit the .uproject
ops.doc:
The plugins: which are enabled now, and what the .uproject lists. With `enable`/`disable`, edit the .uproject
(applies at the next editor start: restart_required).

Args: enable, disable: plugin names (as in their .uplugin, e.g. "MovieRenderPipeline", "PythonScriptPlugin").
prefix: only list enabled plugins whose name starts with this.
Returns: {"enabled": [names], "project": {name: on}, "changed": [names], "restart_required": bool}.
Example: film-ue op editor.plugins 'enable=["MovieRenderPipeline"]'

ops.name: editor.project_setting
ops.summary: Read or set one project setting in the project's Config/Default<file>.ini (what Project Settings writes);
ops.doc:
Read or set one project setting in the project's Config/Default<file>.ini (what Project Settings writes);
applies at the next editor start (restart_required when it changed). For a live change of a console variable
use editor.cvar; this one makes it the project's default.

Args: file: Engine|Game|Editor|Input|... (Config/Default<file>.ini). section: e.g. "/Script/Engine.RendererSettings"
or "/Script/LinuxTargetPlatform.LinuxTargetSettings". key: e.g. "r.RayTracing". value: omit to read.
Returns: {"file", "section", "key", "value", "before", "changed", "restart_required"}.
Example: film-ue op editor.project_setting section=/Script/Engine.RendererSettings key=r.RayTracing value=True

ops.name: editor.wait_compile
ops.summary: Wait until the editor has no shader compiling (no ShaderCompileWorker for `settle_s` seconds), ticking all the
ops.doc:
Wait until the editor has no shader compiling (no ShaderCompileWorker for `settle_s` seconds), ticking all the
while, then (finish) let the engine finish any asset compilation left. The first open of a project on a new box
compiles for many minutes: run this before stills or renders.

Args: timeout_s: give up after this long (an error with code "timeout"). settle_s: how long the workers must
stay at zero. finish: then call the engine's finish-all-compilation (blocks briefly).
Returns: {"waited_s", "workers_max", "finished": bool}. Multi-tick (reports progress).
Example: film-ue op editor.wait_compile timeout_s=3600

ops.name: env.apply
ops.summary: Converge the level to an ENVIRONMENT (or LIGHTING) spec: diff it against env.describe, run only the needed
ops.doc:
Converge the level to an ENVIRONMENT (or LIGHTING) spec: diff it against env.describe, run only the needed
env/light ops, re-describe and confirm a second plan is empty. A multi-tick job. Remembers the spec so
env.mood can switch its moods later.

Args: spec: the spec object (kind environment|lighting, version 1, name, preset?, sections...; environment.md).
mood: one of the spec's `moods` (overrides spec.mood). dry_run: only plan.
Returns: {"changed", "steps": [{"op", "why", "changed"}], "converged", "remaining": [steps]}.
Example: film-ue op env.apply 'spec={"kind":"environment","name":"day","preset":"exterior_golden"}'

ops.name: env.atmosphere
ops.summary: A physical sky (Env_Atmosphere, SkyAtmosphere): Earth by default, with presets and multipliers; converges.
ops.doc:
A physical sky (Env_Atmosphere, SkyAtmosphere): Earth by default, with presets and multipliers; converges.

Args: preset: clear|crisp|hazy|smoggy|dusty. haze: x Mie scattering (aerosols: whiter sky, hazier distance).
rayleigh: x Rayleigh (bluer). aerial_distance_scale: x aerial perspective. mie_anisotropy 0-1. ground_albedo
[r,g,b] linear. The raw engine fields (rayleigh_scattering_scale, mie_scattering_scale, ...) override.
Returns: {"label", "changed", "props": [changed]}.
Example: film-ue op env.atmosphere preset=hazy haze=4

ops.name: env.autoexpose
ops.summary: Closed-loop exposure: measure a region through a camera and change the exposure (or the key light) until the
ops.doc:
Closed-loop exposure: measure a region through a camera and change the exposure (or the key light) until the
region reads at the target, within a tolerance. Converges: already in range -> changed False, no change made.

Args: camera: a camera label. The region: `region` [x0,y0,x1,y1] (0..1, y down), or `subject` (an actor label:
its box from qa.framing; part=face: the top of a standing figure's box), else the whole frame.
target_stops: stops above middle grey (0 = a grey card; skin +0.5..+1; a dark mood -1.5); or target_display
(0-1 display luma). tolerance_stops: how close. adjust: exposure (Env_Post's manual exposure, switching it to
manual if needed) | lights (scale `lights`' intensities, e.g. a rig's key: ["Host_Key"]).
Returns: {"changed", "converged", "iterations": [{"setting", "display", "error_stops"}], "before", "after",
"ev100"? (the exposure it ended at), "scale"? (the light scale applied)}.
Example: film-ue op env.autoexpose camera=HostCam subject=Host part=face target_stops=0.7

ops.name: env.captures_rebuild
ops.summary: Rebuild the reflection captures. The only scriptable route runs a lighting build first
ops.doc:
Rebuild the reflection captures. The only scriptable route runs a lighting build first
(LevelEditorSubsystem.build_light_maps with captures; there is no console command), so it is slow on a level
with static lighting; with Lumen-only levels it is quick. A multi-tick job.

Args: quality: preview|medium|high|production (the lighting build's quality).
Returns: {"changed": True, "built": bool}.
Example: film-ue op env.captures_rebuild

ops.name: env.check
ops.summary: A numeric verdict on a look: meter through `camera` (env.meter) or read a still `png` on the box (any
ops.doc:
A numeric verdict on a look: meter through `camera` (env.meter) or read a still `png` on the box (any
look.still / render frame), and compare with targets: mean [lo,hi] (display luma), median, clipped_max,
crushed_max, cast_max, warm [lo,hi], ev100 [lo,hi] (scene), range_stops_max, stops_over [lo,hi]. Defaults: a
natural, well exposed frame. A multi-tick job.

Args: targets, or `spec` (its checks: {camera, targets}). step: png subsampling.
Returns: {"pass", "issues": [{code, severity, message, fix, value, expected}], "metrics": {...}}.
Example: film-ue op env.check camera=HostCam 'targets={"mean":[0.3,0.5],"clipped_max":0.01}'

ops.name: env.clouds
ops.summary: Volumetric clouds (Env_Clouds): a layer from `bottom_km` up `height_km`, in the engine's simple cloud
ops.doc:
Volumetric clouds (Env_Clouds): a layer from `bottom_km` up `height_km`, in the engine's simple cloud
material or `material`; converges. Needs a SkyAtmosphere (env.atmosphere) to look right.

Returns: {"label", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op env.clouds bottom_km=1.5 height_km=4

ops.name: env.cvars
ops.summary: Set console variables in the editor (they last until the editor restarts; render jobs take theirs from the
ops.doc:
Set console variables in the editor (they last until the editor restarts; render jobs take theirs from the
quality preset: env.quality returns them for render.* cvar lists). Converges: only differing ones are sent.

Args: cvars: {name: value}. Returns: {"changed", "set": {name: [before, after]}}.
Example: film-ue op env.cvars 'cvars={"r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing":1}'

ops.name: env.describe
ops.summary: The environment as numbers, in the same terms as the env/light ops and the spec: sun, moon (elevation,
ops.doc:
The environment as numbers, in the same terms as the env/light ops and the spec: sun, moon (elevation,
azimuth, lux, K), atmosphere, clouds, sky light, hdri, fog, the post fields Env_Post overrides (exposure, grade,
quality) with the EV100 it exposes for, cvars, reflection captures, every light, rigs, lighting channels, and
which spec owns each actor. The state env.apply / film-ue plan diff against.

Returns: {"sun", "moon", "atmosphere", "clouds", "sky_light", "hdri", "fog", "post", "post_owned_fields",
"exposure", "cvars", "captures", "lights", "rigs", "channels", "owners", "other": {...}}.
Example: film-ue op env.describe

ops.name: env.exposure
ops.summary: Exposure on Env_Post, in photographic EV100 (what a light meter says), converges.
ops.doc:
Exposure on Env_Post, in photographic EV100 (what a light meter says), converges.

Args: mode: manual (fixed: expose a scene metering `ev100`; physical camera exposure off, so a camera's
aperture never changes brightness) | physical (the camera's fstop/shutter_s/iso decide; the cine camera's own
aperture overrides fstop) | auto (histogram, adapting within min_ev100..max_ev100 at `speed`). ev100: e.g. 14-15
sunny, 12 overcast, 8-9 bright interior/studio, 5 dim room, 1 stylised moonlight; 'auto' = from the key light
or sun lux in the level spec. compensation: stops brighter (+)/darker (-).
Returns: {"changed", "fields": {...}, "ev100": the scene EV100 exposed for}.
Example: film-ue op env.exposure mode=manual ev100=8.5

ops.name: env.fog
ops.summary: Height fog and volumetric fog (Env_Fog): haze for depth and light shafts; a preset plus overrides; converges.
ops.doc:
Height fog and volumetric fog (Env_Fog): haze for depth and light shafts; a preset plus overrides; converges.

Args: preset: none|light|haze|mist|dense|ground|interior_haze. density, falloff (height falloff), height_cm
(the fog's base), start_cm, max_opacity 0-1, cutoff_cm, color (inscattering, linear), volumetric (bool),
albedo [r,g,b], extinction, distance_cm (volumetric range), scattering (-0.9..0.9, + forward), emissive.
Returns: {"label", "changed", "props": [changed]}.
Example: film-ue op env.fog preset=interior_haze extinction=0.1

ops.name: env.grade
ops.summary: A colour grade on Env_Post: a preset (neutral clean warm_film teal_orange bleach_bypass noir_bw golden_hour
ops.doc:
A colour grade on Env_Post: a preset (neutral clean warm_film teal_orange bleach_bypass noir_bw golden_hour
moonlight pastel high_contrast vintage_fade documentary) plus overrides; re-grading resets the old preset's
fields (every grade starts from neutral). Converges.

Args: fields: friendly names or PostProcessSettings fields: white_balance (K), tint, saturation/contrast/
gamma/gain/offset (a number or [r,g,b]; also color_<wheel>_shadows/_midtones/_highlights), bloom, grain,
vignette, fringe, lut (a texture path) and lut_intensity, film_slope/toe/shoulder/black_clip/white_clip.
Returns: {"changed", "set": [fields]}.
Example: film-ue op env.grade preset=teal_orange 'fields={"vignette":0.2,"white_balance":6000}'

ops.name: env.hdri
ops.summary: Light (and optionally surround) the scene with an HDRI: the sky light from the cubemap, and with `backdrop`
ops.doc:
Light (and optionally surround) the scene with an HDRI: the sky light from the cubemap, and with `backdrop`
an HDRIBackdrop (Env_HDRI: a projected dome, needs the HDRIBackdrop plugin). A multi-tick job; converges.

Args: cubemap: a TextureCube path (import an .hdr as a long-lat cubemap). intensity: sky light scale.
rotation_deg: yaw of the image. backdrop: also show it. size_cm: the dome's size.
Returns: {"changed", "sky_light": {...}, "backdrop": label|None, "warnings": [...]}.
Example: film-ue op env.hdri cubemap=/Game/HDRI/T_Courtyard intensity=1 rotation_deg=90

ops.name: env.meter
ops.summary: Meter the scene through a camera without a viewport: a scene capture in linear HDR (SceneColorHDR, read back
ops.doc:
Meter the scene through a camera without a viewport: a scene capture in linear HDR (SceneColorHDR, read back
raw, unclamped) gives the scene's luminance statistics and the EV100 a reflected meter would choose; a second in
final colour gives the image's brightness, clipping, crush and colour cast. A multi-tick job (a few ticks).

Args: camera: a camera actor label. width/height: capture size (small is enough for statistics).
exposure_ev100: compare the scene with this exposure (default: what Env_Post exposes for, if manual).
region: only this box [x0, y0, x1, y1] (0..1, y down), e.g. a face box from qa.framing (spot metering).
Returns: {"scene": scene_stats, "display": display_stats, "camera", "fov_deg", "region"}.
Example: film-ue op env.meter camera=HostCam

ops.name: env.mood
ops.summary: Switch the last applied spec `spec_name` to one of its moods (day/night, ...): env.apply with that mood;
ops.doc:
Switch the last applied spec `spec_name` to one of its moods (day/night, ...): env.apply with that mood;
`mood` None goes back to the spec's own mood. A multi-tick job.

Returns: env.apply's result plus {"mood"}.
Example: film-ue op env.mood mood=night spec_name=studio

ops.name: env.moon
ops.summary: A moon (Env_Moon): a second atmosphere light (index 1) for night, dim and cool; converges.
ops.doc:
A moon (Env_Moon): a second atmosphere light (index 1) for night, dim and cool; converges.

Args: elevation_deg, azimuth_deg (compass), north_yaw_deg. intensity_lux: 'auto' = 0.5 (a full moon is ~0.25;
stylised nights use 0.5-2 with a low exposure). temperature_k: 'auto' = 4100. softness_deg: angular size.
Returns: like env.sun.
Example: film-ue op env.moon elevation_deg=40 azimuth_deg=135 intensity_lux=1.0

ops.name: env.plan
ops.summary: What env.apply would do: the op calls that converge the level to an environment/lighting spec, without
ops.doc:
What env.apply would do: the op calls that converge the level to an environment/lighting spec, without
doing them. Errors name the spec field (did-you-mean) before anything changes.

Returns: {"steps": [{"op", "args", "why"}], "converged": bool}.
Example: film-ue op env.plan 'spec={"kind":"environment","name":"day","preset":"exterior_day"}'

ops.name: env.post
ops.summary: Set PostProcessSettings fields on the environment's unbound volume (Env_Post), each override flag set for
ops.doc:
Set PostProcessSettings fields on the environment's unbound volume (Env_Post), each override flag set for
you; `clear` turns fields' overrides off. Converges; reports what changed.

Args: fields: {snake_case field: value}: numbers, bools, [r,g,b(,a)] colours and colour wheels, enum strings
"AutoExposureMethod.AEM_MANUAL", texture paths for LUTs. clear: field names to stop overriding.
priority: the volume's priority (1 wins over default-priority volumes).
Returns: {"label", "changed", "set": [fields], "cleared": [fields]}.
Example: film-ue op env.post 'fields={"bloom_intensity":0.3,"vignette_intensity":0.2}'

ops.name: env.preset
ops.summary: Build a whole, consistent environment from a named preset (sky, sun, fog, exposure, grade, quality together):
ops.doc:
Build a whole, consistent environment from a named preset (sky, sun, fog, exposure, grade, quality together):
exterior_day exterior_golden exterior_overcast exterior_blue_hour exterior_night interior_day interior_night
studio_black studio_grey. The same as env.apply of {kind: environment, name: owner, preset: name, ...overrides};
re-running converges, switching presets replaces only what differs. A multi-tick job.

Args: name: the preset (env.presets lists them with their lux and EV100). owner: the spec name it is kept under
(env.mood and prune use it). overrides: spec sections over the preset, e.g. {"sun": {"time": "10:00"}}.
Returns: env.apply's result.
Example: film-ue op env.preset name=exterior_golden 'overrides={"fog":{"preset":"mist"}}'

ops.name: env.presets
ops.summary: Every named thing the env/light ops and specs take, with what it is for: environment presets, times of day,
ops.doc:
Every named thing the env/light ops and specs take, with what it is for: environment presets, times of day,
atmosphere and fog presets, grades, quality presets, rig presets and roles, practical types.

Example: film-ue op env.presets

ops.name: env.quality
ops.summary: Lumen / virtual shadow map / hardware ray tracing quality: preset preview|draft|final|cinematic|no_gi plus
ops.doc:
Lumen / virtual shadow map / hardware ray tracing quality: preset preview|draft|final|cinematic|no_gi plus
overrides (gi none|lumen, reflections none|lumen|ssr, shadows vsm|maps, hwrt bool, hit_lighting
none|reflections|all, lumen {final_gather, reflection, scene_detail, scene_lighting, max_trace_distance},
fog_grid [pixel, z], vsm_bias, megalights, cvars). Sets the cvars now and the post fields on Env_Post.

Args: project: also make it the project's default (GI, reflections, VSM, HWRT, mesh distance fields) in
Config/DefaultEngine.ini through editor.project_setting; applies at the next editor start (restart_required).
HWRT also needs r.RayTracing=True there (editor.project_setting key=r.RayTracing value=True). Returns: {"changed", "cvars": {...}, "post": [...],
"render_cvars": [ "name value", ... ] (to pass to a render job), "project_settings", "restart_required"}.
Example: film-ue op env.quality preset=cinematic

ops.name: env.reflection_capture
ops.summary: A reflection capture (a fallback for reflections Lumen cannot trace, and for translucency): a sphere with an
ops.doc:
A reflection capture (a fallback for reflections Lumen cannot trace, and for translucency): a sphere with an
influence radius, or a box whose half-size is `extent_cm` (the actor's scale; ReflectionCaptureComponent.cpp:1358);
converges. Captures update with env.captures_rebuild.

Returns: {"label", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op env.reflection_capture label=RoomCapture shape=box 'loc=[0,0,150]' 'extent_cm=[400,300,150]'

ops.name: env.remove
ops.summary: Remove environment parts the ops made (sun moon atmosphere clouds sky_light hdri fog post), or everything an
ops.doc:
Remove environment parts the ops made (sun moon atmosphere clouds sky_light hdri fog post), or everything an
`owner` (spec name) made with no `parts`. Missing parts are fine; actors the ops did not make are never removed.

Returns: {"changed", "removed": [labels]}.
Example: film-ue op env.remove 'parts=["fog","clouds"]'

ops.name: env.schema
ops.summary: The JSON Schema of the environment or lighting spec (the same one in tools/filmtools/unreal/schemas/).
ops.doc:
The JSON Schema of the environment or lighting spec (the same one in tools/filmtools/unreal/schemas/).

Example: film-ue op env.schema kind=lighting

ops.name: env.sky_light
ops.summary: The sky light (Env_SkyLight): ambient light from the sky, real-time captured (with an atmosphere), captured
ops.doc:
The sky light (Env_SkyLight): ambient light from the sky, real-time captured (with an atmosphere), captured
once from the scene, or from a cubemap (an HDRI); converges and recaptures when it changed. A multi-tick job.

Args: mode: realtime|captured|cubemap (default realtime with an atmosphere, else captured). intensity: scale.
cubemap: a TextureCube path (mode cubemap). cubemap_angle_deg: its yaw. lower_hemisphere_black/_color.
Returns: {"label", "changed", "mode"}.
Example: film-ue op env.sky_light mode=cubemap cubemap=/Game/HDRI/T_Studio intensity=1.2

ops.name: env.sun
ops.summary: The sun (Env_Sun): placed by local time and place (NOAA solar position), a named time of day, or an explicit
ops.doc:
The sun (Env_Sun): placed by local time and place (NOAA solar position), a named time of day, or an explicit
elevation/azimuth; converges.

Args: time: 'HH:MM', decimal hours, or a name (dawn sunrise golden_morning morning noon afternoon golden_evening
sunset blue_hour dusk night). lat/lon (deg, east +), date 'YYYY-MM-DD', tz (hours east of UTC): with these the
position is astronomical (and a name is solved for that day: golden_evening = when the sun is 6 deg up).
elevation_deg/azimuth_deg (compass, clockwise from north) override. north_yaw_deg: the level yaw of north
(0 = +X). intensity_lux: 'auto' = 120000 under a SkyAtmosphere (it attenuates and tints), else clear-sky by
elevation. temperature_k: 'auto' = 6500 with an atmosphere, else by elevation. softness_deg: angular size.
Returns: {"label", "changed", "elevation_deg", "azimuth_deg", "intensity_lux", "temperature_k", "hour"?}.
Example: film-ue op env.sun time=golden_evening lat=19.07 lon=72.88 date=2026-11-05 tz=5.5

ops.name: fab.add
ops.summary: Add a Fab asset to the project from its signed download URL (what the Fab page hands the plugin's
ops.doc:
Add a Fab asset to the project from its signed download URL (what the Fab page hands the plugin's
AddToProject; tools/filmtools/unreal/fab_shim.py gets it for a listing without a window): download (no auth:
the URL is signed), unzip into the plugin's cache, import as fab.import does. With the FabScript project plugin
installed (unreal/plugins/FabScript) and metadata given, Epic's own AddToProject runs instead, for every format
(including unreal-engine packs).

Multi-tick: downloads in the background and yields until done.
Args: url: the signed download URL. metadata: {"AssetId", "AssetName", "AssetType" (gltf|fbx|unreal-engine|...),
      "ListingType", "AssetNamespace", "DistributionPointBaseUrls", "IsQuixel"} as the page gives it.
      dest: content folder. replace: import again over an earlier import.
Returns: fab.import's result plus {"download": file on the box, "route": "python"|"native"}.
Example: film-ue op fab.add url=<signed url> 'metadata={"AssetId": "abc", "AssetName": "Rock", "IsQuixel": true}'

ops.name: fab.import
ops.summary: Import a Fab or Megascans download that is on the box (a zip, or a folder): Fab-plugin format (one .gltf +
ops.doc:
Import a Fab or Megascans download that is on the box (a zip, or a folder): Fab-plugin format (one .gltf +
.json) the way the plugin does it (Interchange with InterchangeMegascansPipeline, per type: 3D Nanite, plants,
surfaces, decals), any other glTF/FBX/OBJ/USD with the generic importer, loose textures as a PBR material.

Args: path: zip or folder on the box (e.g. /tmp/FabLibrary/<AssetId>/x.zip). dest: content folder (default
      /Game/Fab/Megascans/<Type>/<Name>_<id>/<Tier> like the plugin, or /Game/Fab/<Name>). kind: force the
      Megascans type (3D, Plants, Surfaces, Decals, Imperfections). replace: re-import over what is there (else
      an imported asset is kept: changed false).
Returns: {"format", "dest", "imported": [paths], "material": path|None, "changed", "meta"}.
Example: film-ue op fab.import path=/data/fab/rock_4k.zip

ops.name: fab.library
ops.summary: The signed-in account's Fab library (what it owns), from the endpoint the plugin's My Folder uses
ops.doc:
The signed-in account's Fab library (what it owns), from the endpoint the plugin's My Folder uses
(GET <fab>/e/accounts/<account>/ue/library, FabMyFolderIntegration.cpp): title, asset id, listing type, the
page url, and a thumbnail url.

Args: query: keep items whose title/description contain these words. limit: at most this many. account_id: the
      Epic account (default: from the token).
Returns: {"items": [{"title", "asset_id", "asset_namespace", "listing_type", "url", "image", "source"}],
         "count", "next_cursor"}.
Example: film-ue op fab.library query=chair

ops.name: fab.login
ops.summary: Sign Fab in: by default with the saved sign-in (opening a Fab tab is what makes the plugin try it, and then
ops.doc:
Sign Fab in: by default with the saved sign-in (opening a Fab tab is what makes the plugin try it, and then
the editor's -AUTH_TYPE=exchangecode -AUTH_PASSWORD=<code> if that fails); with portal, start the device-code
sign-in (Fab.Login): its code and URL are in the editor log for a person to approve once.

Multi-tick: waits up to timeout_s for the sign-in. Already signed in: changes nothing.
Args: portal: device-code sign-in instead of the saved one. timeout_s: how long to wait.
Returns: {"signed_in", "changed", "method", "waited_s", "hint"}.
Example: film-ue op fab.login

ops.name: fab.status
ops.summary: Is Fab usable from code here: plugin loaded, signed in, a saved sign-in on disk, the pack installer library
ops.doc:
Is Fab usable from code here: plugin loaded, signed in, a saved sign-in on disk, the pack installer library
(Linux needs ThirdParty/libBuildPatchInstallerLib.so for unreal-engine-format packs), the download cache.

Returns: {"plugin", "signed_in", "saved_sign_ins": int, "pack_installer": bool, "cache_dir", "platform",
         "next": what to do}. No token is returned.
Example: film-ue op fab.status

ops.name: foliage.describe
ops.summary: The scatters in the project (or one): their arguments, seed, foliage types and instance counts as placed,
ops.doc:
The scatters in the project (or one): their arguments, seed, foliage types and instance counts as placed,
and the foliage instances in the level now per mesh (`measured`), so a lost or doubled scatter shows.

Example: film-ue op foliage.describe prefix=Lawn

ops.name: foliage.pcg
ops.summary: Run a PCG graph on an actor with a PCG component, with parameters and a seed, and wait until it has generated.
ops.doc:
Run a PCG graph on an actor with a PCG component, with parameters and a seed, and wait until it has generated.
With `loc` (and `extent_cm`, the half size) a PCG Volume named `label` is made there first if missing.

Args: graph: a PCG graph asset (/Game/...; keep the actor's own when ""). seed: the component's seed.
params: {graph parameter: value} (bool, int, float, string, [x, y, z], or an asset path).
Returns: {"label", "graph", "seed", "generated", "instances": ISM instances on the actor, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op foliage.pcg label=PCG_Forest graph=/Game/PCG/PG_Forest seed=3 'params={"Density":0.6}'

ops.name: foliage.pcg_clear
ops.summary: Clear what a PCG component generated (and delete the actor with `delete`). Missing actors are fine.
ops.doc:
Clear what a PCG component generated (and delete the actor with `delete`). Missing actors are fine.

Example: film-ue op foliage.pcg_clear label=PCG_Forest

ops.name: foliage.remove
ops.summary: Remove a scatter: its instances and its foliage types (removing nothing is fine).
ops.doc:
Remove a scatter: its instances and its foliage types (removing nothing is fine).

Example: film-ue op foliage.remove prefix=Lawn

ops.name: foliage.scatter
ops.summary: Scatter meshes over a region as foliage instances, the same for the same seed; re-running converges (the
ops.doc:
Scatter meshes over a region as foliage instances, the same for the same seed; re-running converges (the
scatter's own instances are replaced; nothing else is touched).

Args: prefix: the scatter's name (its foliage types live in /Game/_Foliage/<prefix>/). meshes: [{"mesh":
"/Game/...", "weight": 1, "scale": [lo, hi], "height_jitter": [lo, hi], "tilt_deg": 0, "yaw": "random" | [lo, hi]
| deg, "z_offset_cm": 0, "align_to_normal": false}]. region: {"rect": [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]]} | {"circle": [cx, cy,
r]} | {"ring": [cx, cy, r0, r1]} | {"polygon": [[x, y], ...]} (cm). count, or density_per_m2. min_dist_cm:
spacing (default from the density). exclude: regions to keep clear; exclude_actors: labels whose footprints
(plus exclude_margin_cm) stay clear. patchiness 0..1 with patch_cm: clumps. surface: "trace" (drop onto what is
below, between trace_from_z_cm and trace_to_z_cm; instances over nothing or steeper than max_slope_deg are
dropped) or "flat" (at z_cm). cull_cm: [start, end] distance culling. force: rewrite even when unchanged.
A multi-tick job (traces yield every 500).
Returns: {"prefix", "changed", "placed", "planned", "dropped": {"no_ground", "too_steep"}, "per_mesh",
"types", "hash", "area_m2"}.
Example: film-ue op foliage.scatter prefix=Lawn seed=7 'meshes=[{"mesh":"/Game/Env/SM_Grass","scale":[0.8,1.2]}]' 'region={"rect":[[-1000,-1000],[1000,1000]]}' density_per_m2=4

ops.name: groom.describe
ops.summary: An actor's grooms as numbers: per component its groom/binding assets, per group the instance overrides
ops.doc:
An actor's grooms as numbers: per component its groom/binding assets, per group the instance overrides
(width_cm, root/tip scale, shadow density, LOD bias, length scale, and whether each is overridden), per material
slot the hair parameters (melanin, redness, roughness, white, light) and every scalar parameter name; plus the
sky-lighting cvar.

Returns: {"label", "components": [{"name", "groom", "binding", "visible", "groups": [...], "materials": [...]}],
"cvars": {"r.HairStrands.SkyLighting"}}.
Example: film-ue op groom.describe label=Ada

ops.name: groom.measure
ops.summary: What the hair looks like, in numbers: per view, the hair's pixels (a groom-only depth capture), its share of
ops.doc:
What the hair looks like, in numbers: per view, the hair's pixels (a groom-only depth capture), its share of
the head's silhouette (thinner or shorter hair shows more scalp/face: a density proxy), and its colour in the lit
scene (mean RGB, stops from mid grey, saturation, hue and its name).

Args: label: the character. component: one groom component (default all). views: around the head from the face
(2: front, back; 4 adds the sides). size_px: capture size. out_dir: write each view's still and mask.
Returns: {"views": {name: {pixels, share_of_head, mean_rgb, stops, saturation, hue, name, box, still?}},
"mean": {...}}. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op groom.measure label=Ada views=4 out_dir=/srv/qa/hair

ops.name: groom.set
ops.summary: Tune hair on one actor, per instance, and (with measure_views) measure it before and after.
ops.doc:
Tune hair on one actor, per instance, and (with measure_views) measure it before and after.

Args: label: the character. component: one groom component (default all: hair, brows, beard, ...). group: one
hair group (default all). width_cm: strand width (cm; MetaHuman scalp hair ~0.005-0.01). root_scale/tip_scale:
width multipliers along the strand. shadow_density: how opaque the hair's self-shadow is (thin hair: lower).
lod_bias: -7..7 (positive: coarser LODs, fewer strands drawn). length_scale: 0..1 of the strand length.
melanin/redness/roughness/white/light: 0..1 hair material parameters (hairMelanin, hairRedness, HairRoughness,
WhiteAmount, LightAmount); dye: [r, g, b] linear (HairDye); params: other material parameters by their names,
{name: number | [r, g, b]}. strand_fraction: 0..1 of the strands (asset decimation; needs edit_asset=true:
rebuilds the groom asset for EVERY actor using it, and is saved only with assets.save). measure_views: measure
with groom.measure before and after (0: no measuring). out_dir: stills of both measurements.
