Returns: {"changed", "groups": {component: {group: {arg: [before, after]}}}, "materials": {component: {slot:
{param: [before, after]}}}, "asset": {...}?, "before"?, "after"?, "delta"?}. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op groom.set label=Ada melanin=0.95 redness=0.1 width_cm=0.008 measure_views=2

ops.name: groom.sky_lighting

ops.name: layout.align
ops.summary: Line actors up along one axis by their bounds: their min edges, max edges or centres on a common value
ops.doc:
Line actors up along one axis by their bounds: their min edges, max edges or centres on a common value
(`ref_cm`, the same edge of `ref_label`, or the group's extreme / mean).

Example: film-ue op layout.align 'labels=["Book_00","Book_01","Book_02"]' axis=y to=max

ops.name: layout.array
ops.summary: Lay out `count` copies of an asset (or a basic shape) as a row, a grid or a circle, labelled
ops.doc:
Lay out `count` copies of an asset (or a basic shape) as a row, a grid or a circle, labelled
`<prefix>_00`, `<prefix>_01`, ...; re-running moves the same actors, and a smaller count removes the extras.

Args: pattern: row (start + k * step_cm), grid (rows of `cols`, X by step_cm[0], Y by step_cm[1]) or circle
(around `center`, radius_cm, from start_deg over arc_deg, counter-clockwise from above). face: none (yaw_deg),
center (circle: each faces the centre), out (faces away). drop: rest each on what is under it.
Returns: {"changed", "labels", "made", "moved", "removed"}.
Example: film-ue op layout.array prefix=Chair asset=/Game/Props/SM_Chair pattern=circle count=6 \
         'center=[0,0,0]' radius_cm=120 face=center

ops.name: layout.distribute
ops.summary: Space actors evenly along an axis, in the order given: centres from start_cm to end_cm (default: the first
ops.doc:
Space actors evenly along an axis, in the order given: centres from start_cm to end_cm (default: the first
and last actors' current centres), or edge to edge `gap_cm` apart starting at the first one.

Example: film-ue op layout.distribute 'labels=["A","B","C","D"]' axis=x gap_cm=20

ops.name: layout.drop
ops.summary: Rest each actor on whatever is under it: its bounds' bottom on the highest support below its centre whose
ops.doc:
Rest each actor on whatever is under it: its bounds' bottom on the highest support below its centre whose
footprint overlaps (a table top, a rug, a riser), else on `floor_z`. Actors are dropped in the order given, so
list a table before the cup that sits on it.

Args: labels: actors to drop. floor_z: the floor height in cm (None for no floor: an actor over nothing stays
put). gap_cm: lift above the support. mode: bounds (boxes, deterministic) or trace (a line trace down; needs
collision).
Returns: {"changed": bool, "moved": {label: dz_cm}, "unsupported": [labels with nothing under them]}.
Example: film-ue op layout.drop 'labels=["Desk","Lamp","Mug"]'

ops.name: layout.relative
ops.summary: Put `label` at an offset in another actor's frame: [forward, right, up] cm from `of` along its own yaw (a
ops.doc:
Put `label` at an offset in another actor's frame: [forward, right, up] cm from `of` along its own yaw (a
chair 80 cm in front of a desk: offset_cm=[80, 0, 0]), then turn it and rest it on what is under it.

Args: face: toward (look at `of`), away, same (copy its yaw), none (keep), or fixed (use yaw_deg).
Returns: {"changed", "loc", "rot"}.
Example: film-ue op layout.relative label=Chair of=Desk 'offset_cm=[80,0,0]' face=toward

ops.name: layout.remove
ops.summary: Remove every actor a layout.array / layout.scatter with this prefix made (by its tag, not by name).
ops.doc:
Remove every actor a layout.array / layout.scatter with this prefix made (by its tag, not by name).

Example: film-ue op layout.remove prefix=Rock

ops.name: layout.scatter
ops.summary: Scatter up to `count` copies of an asset over a rectangle, no two closer than min_dist_cm, deterministic for
ops.doc:
Scatter up to `count` copies of an asset over a rectangle, no two closer than min_dist_cm, deterministic for
a seed (Poisson disk), with random yaw and uniform scale in ranges; labelled `<prefix>_00`...; re-running with
the same seed gives the same layout, a new seed a new one.

Args: region: [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] cm. exclude: rectangles to keep clear ([[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] each). avoid:
actor labels whose footprints (plus min_dist_cm / 2) are kept clear. z: height before dropping. drop: rest each
on what is under it.
Returns: {"changed", "labels", "made", "moved", "removed", "placed": n} (n < count when the region is full).
Example: film-ue op layout.scatter prefix=Rock asset=/Game/Env/SM_Rock count=30 \
         'region=[[-1000,-1000],[1000,1000]]' min_dist_cm=150 seed=7 'avoid=["Path"]'

ops.name: layout.settle
ops.summary: Let props fall and come to rest under physics, then keep where they landed (a pile of books, a dropped
ops.doc:
Let props fall and come to rest under physics, then keep where they landed (a pile of books, a dropped
cushion, a chair knocked over): runs Simulate in Editor for `seconds`, reads each actor's resting transform from
the simulated world and writes it back onto the editor actor. Multi-tick. The actors' meshes need collision, and
so does what they land on.

Args: labels: actors to simulate (made Movable, physics on for the run; restored after unless keep_physics).
seconds: simulated time to let them settle. start_timeout_s: how long to wait for Simulate to start.
Returns: {"changed", "moved": {label: {"loc", "rot", "dist_cm"}}, "still": [labels that did not move > 0.5 cm]}.
Example: film-ue op layout.settle 'labels=["Book_00","Book_01","Cushion"]' seconds=3

directional), temperature or colour, size, cone, radius, channels, owner/role/rig; with `at` [x,y,z] also what

ops.name: light.rig
ops.summary: Light a subject with a named rig (key/fill/rim/...) placed around it relative to the camera, intensities from
ops.doc:
Light a subject with a named rig (key/fill/rim/...) placed around it relative to the camera, intensities from
the key's lux at the subject and the lighting ratio; converges (re-running moves/retunes, a dropped role is removed).

Args: subject: an actor label or [x,y,z] cm (a label lights ~eye height of its bounds, or `socket`, or its
location + `subject_offset`). camera: a label or [x,y,z] (else `facing_yaw_deg`). preset: env.presets rigs
(three_point, interview, loop, rembrandt, butterfly, clamshell, split, high_key, low_key, noir, silhouette,
window). key_lux: lux on the subject from the key. ratio: (key+fill):fill, 2 flat .. 8 noir. lights: per-role
overrides {"rim": {"rel": 1.5}, "fill": null, "kicker": {}} (fields: angle side elevation distance width height
cone temperature color rel lux candelas shadows channels). prefix: label prefix (lights are <prefix><Role>).
key_side: left|right (camera-left/right), or short|broad (from the subject's facing: `facing_yaw_deg` or the
subject actor's yaw, +X its front; short keys the side of the face turned away from the lens). scale: x distances/sizes. temperature_k/channels: for every light.
Returns: {"changed", "lights": [labels], "removed": [labels], "subject_point", "camera_point",
"measured": {"lux", "per_light", "ratio"}}.

Prefer light.add (lux, candelas, converging).
Example: film-ue op look.light label=Key kind=rect 'loc=[150,120,230]' 'look_at=[0,0,165]' intensity=9

ops.name: look.material
ops.summary: A material instance: kind Surface (color, roughness, metallic, specular), Textured (a texture tinted by color,
ops.doc:
A material instance: kind Surface (color, roughness, metallic, specular), Textured (a texture tinted by color,
tiled), Screen (an emitted texture x intensity behind glossy glass), Emissive (color x intensity, unlit), Glass
(translucent, opacity), ScreenBlink (Screen with a baked-in cursor that blinks: scalars Blink 0-1 and the cursor's
UV rectangle CursorU0, CursorU1, CursorV0, CursorV1), Pbr (texture, normal and mask maps; mask R x roughness,
G x metallic), PbrMasked (Pbr cut out by the texture's alpha), Sheer (backlit thin fabric: mask B x opacity,
dithered; transmission colour, glow), Glow (texture x color x intensity, additive) or GlowWipe (Glow revealed
left to right: scalars Reveal 0-1 and Softness; it also takes the lower of Reveal and MPC_FM's WipeReveal, and is
multiplied by MPC_FM's WipeOn, both 1 unless a sequence keys them). `scalars` sets any other scalar parameters by
name. Colours are linear. Re-running updates it.
Prefer mat.* (WP2) for new materials.
Example: film-ue op look.material name=MI_Wall 'color=[0.6,0.55,0.5]' roughness=0.8

ops.name: look.post
ops.summary: An unbound post-process volume; `settings` are PostProcessSettings fields (each override flag set for you).
ops.doc:
An unbound post-process volume; `settings` are PostProcessSettings fields (each override flag set for you).
Prefer env.post / env.exposure / env.grade.

ops.name: look.sky
ops.summary: Daylight: a sun (directional light, `lux`) from `azimuth` degrees (0 = shining along +X, i.e. from behind the
ops.doc:
Daylight: a sun (directional light, `lux`) from `azimuth` degrees (0 = shining along +X, i.e. from behind the
back wall towards the camera; 90 = shining along +Y) and `elevation` above the horizon, a sky atmosphere and a
real-time captured sky light. `shadow_softness` is the sun's source angle in degrees.
Prefer env.sun / env.atmosphere / env.sky_light (time of day, place).
Example: film-ue op look.sky elevation=28 azimuth=-28 lux=17000

ops.name: look.slots
ops.summary: An actor's material slots by name ({slot: material}); `materials` sets those named (unknown names are
ops.doc:
An actor's material slots by name ({slot: material}); `materials` sets those named (unknown names are
reported, not guessed).
Example: film-ue op look.slots label=Chair 'materials={"Seat":"/Game/FM/Materials/MI_Leather"}'

ops.name: look.still
ops.summary: A still through a camera at the viewport's quality, written to `path` on the workstation (png). A multi-tick
ops.doc:
A still through a camera at the viewport's quality, written to `path` on the workstation (png). A multi-tick
job: it returns once the file is on disk.
Example: film-ue op look.still camera_label=Cam path=/tmp/still.png

ops.name: mat.assign
ops.summary: Set a material on a mesh ASSET's slot (every actor showing the mesh changes). For one actor only use
ops.doc:
Set a material on a mesh ASSET's slot (every actor showing the mesh changes). For one actor only use
level.material.

Args: mesh: /Game/... StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh. material: /Game/... material or instance. slot: index or slot
      name.
Returns: {"mesh", "slot", "slot_name", "material", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op mat.assign mesh=/Game/Props/SM_Chair material=/Game/Mats/MI_Oak slot=0

ops.name: mat.check
ops.summary: Does a material render as meant: it compiles (else the engine draws its checker), and every texture it uses
ops.doc:
Does a material render as meant: it compiles (else the engine draws its checker), and every texture it uses
has the compression its sampler needs (a normal map TC_NORMALMAP, a data map TC_MASKS and linear, a colour map
sRGB and neither).

Args: path: /Game/... of a Material or instance.
Returns: {"pass", "issues": [{"code": material.not_compiling | material.texture_kind, "severity", "message",
         "fix", "subject", "value", "expected"}], "metrics": {"num_samplers", ..., "textures_checked"}}.
Example: film-ue op mat.check path=/Game/Mats/MI_Rock

ops.name: mat.describe
ops.summary: A material or instance as JSON: class, parent chain, library master (if any), blend/shading, every parameter
ops.doc:
A material or instance as JSON: class, parent chain, library master (if any), blend/shading, every parameter
with its current value, compile statistics, and which actors in the open level draw it.

Args: path: /Game/... of a Material or MaterialInstance.
Returns: {"path", "class", "chain": [paths], "master", "blend", "shading", "two_sided", "params": {name:
         {"kind", "value"}}, "stats", "users": [labels], "fingerprint": the spec hash it was built from (mat.graph,
         mat.master) or null}.
Example: film-ue op mat.describe path=/Game/Mats/MI_RedPaint

ops.name: mat.graph
ops.summary: Build a Material from a node-graph spec (material by spec); re-running the same spec changes nothing.
ops.doc:
Build a Material from a node-graph spec (material by spec); re-running the same spec changes nothing.

spec: {"blend": opaque|masked|translucent|additive|modulate, "shading": default_lit|unlit|subsurface|
subsurface_profile|two_sided_foliage|cloth|clear_coat|thin_translucent|hair|eye, "two_sided": bool,
"domain": surface|deferred_decal|post_process|light_function|ui, "translucency_lighting": surface_per_pixel|...,
"usage": [skeletal_mesh, instanced, nanite, groom, morph_targets, ...], "opacity_mask_clip": 0.333,
"nodes": {id: {"type": Scalar|Vector|Texture|Switch|Const|Multiply|Add|Lerp|OneMinus|Power|TexCoord|Fresnel|
VertexColor|Function|... or any MaterialExpression class, "in": {pin: "node" | "node.R" | number | [r,g,b]},
other keys: editor properties (name, default, texture, sampler: color|normal|masks|linear_color|grayscale)}},
"outputs": {BaseColor|Metallic|Specular|Roughness|EmissiveColor|Opacity|OpacityMask|Normal|SubsurfaceColor|
AmbientOcclusion|Refraction|WorldPositionOffset|CustomData0|...: source}}.
The spec is checked before anything is touched (unknown node/pin/source -> bad_args with near names). A
material drawn in the open level is not rebuilt (conflict) unless force.
Args: path: /Game/... of the Material. spec: as above. rebuild: even if unchanged. save: save the asset.
Returns: {"path", "changed", "fingerprint", "nodes", "stats": {"num_samplers", "num_pixel_shader_instructions"}}.
Example: film-ue op mat.graph path=/Game/Mats/M_Stripes 'spec={"nodes": {"c": {"type": "Vector", "name": "Col",
         "default": [1, 0, 0, 1]}}, "outputs": {"BaseColor": "c"}}'

ops.name: mat.instance
ops.summary: Make or update a material instance: its parent, and parameters from a dict; only what differs is written.
ops.doc:
Make or update a material instance: its parent, and parameters from a dict; only what differs is written.

Args: path: /Game/... of the instance. master: a library master by name (mat.masters: opaque, glass, emissive,
      ...; built on demand) or parent: any material/instance path. params: {name: value}: a number (scalar), a
      list [r, g, b(, a)] linear (vector), a /Game texture path (texture), true/false (static switch). Names are
      checked against the parent's parameters. force: reparent even if the open level draws it (unsafe).
Returns: {"path", "parent", "changed", "updated": [what was written]}.
Example: film-ue op mat.instance path=/Game/Mats/MI_RedPaint master=opaque
         'params={"Tint": [0.6, 0.05, 0.04], "Roughness": 0.35}'

ops.name: mat.master
ops.summary: Build (or keep) one library master material in /Game/FM/Lib, with its default textures.
ops.doc:
Build (or keep) one library master material in /Game/FM/Lib, with its default textures.

A master already built from the same spec is left alone (changed false). One built from an older spec is
rebuilt in place, but only when nothing in the open level draws it (recompiling a drawn material can crash the
editor): otherwise it fails with code conflict, unless force.
Args: name: a master from mat.masters (opaque, opaque_orm, masked, masked_orm, foliage, glass, emissive, screen,
      cloth, skin, unlit, decal). rebuild: rebuild even if current. force: skip the drawn-by check.
Returns: {"path", "changed", "fingerprint", "nodes", "stats"}.
Example: film-ue op mat.master name=opaque_orm

ops.name: mat.masters
ops.summary: The library's master materials: what each is for, its path, whether it is built and current, and its
ops.doc:
The library's master materials: what each is for, its path, whether it is built and current, and its
parameters with what they do.

Args: name: one master (else all).
Returns: {master: {"path", "description", "built": bool, "current": bool, "params": {name: {"kind",
         "default", "doc"}}}}.
Example: film-ue op mat.masters name=glass

ops.name: mat.pbr
ops.summary: A PBR material instance from a texture set: imports the files (or takes textures already in the project),
ops.doc:
A PBR material instance from a texture set: imports the files (or takes textures already in the project),
sets each texture's sRGB/compression by its role, picks the master (opaque, opaque_orm for a packed ORM map,
masked/foliage for cut-outs) and wires every map in.

Args: path: /Game/... of the instance. maps: {role: texture path or file}: roles base_color, normal, orm,
      roughness, metallic, ao, opacity, translucency, emissive, gloss (inverted into roughness is not
      supported: convert it first). files: files on the box (a texture set; roles from their names, e.g.
      T_Rock_BaseColor.png, T_Rock_Normal.png, T_Rock_ORM.png). folder: a folder on the box holding one set.
      texture_dest: where textures are imported (default: the instance's folder + /Textures). cutout: use the
      masked master (opacity map, or base colour alpha). foliage: the foliage master. params: other master
      parameters (Tint, Tiling, NormalStrength, ...).
Returns: {"path", "master", "maps": {role: texture path}, "changed", "imported": [paths], "ignored": [files]}.
Example: film-ue op mat.pbr path=/Game/Mats/MI_Rock folder=/data/megascans/rock_4k

ops.name: mat.preset
ops.summary: A ready-made material: an instance of a library master with a named look (chrome, gold, glass_clear, water,
ops.doc:
A ready-made material: an instance of a library master with a named look (chrome, gold, glass_clear, water,
plastic_gloss, rubber, emissive_panel, screen, ...), adjusted by a few plain arguments.

Args: path: /Game/... of the instance. name: a preset (mat.presets lists them with their master and values).

      emitted luminance in cd/m2 for emissive/screen presets. params: any other master parameters.
Returns: mat.instance's result plus {"preset", "master"}.
Example: film-ue op mat.preset path=/Game/Mats/MI_Panel name=emissive_panel nits=400 'color=[1, 0.9, 0.8]'

ops.name: mat.presets
ops.summary: The named looks mat.preset makes: {name: {"master", "params"}}.
ops.doc:
The named looks mat.preset makes: {name: {"master", "params"}}.

Example: film-ue op mat.presets

ops.name: mh.add
ops.summary: Make a MetaHuman character asset (or keep the one at `path`): copied from a preset, from another character,
ops.doc:
Make a MetaHuman character asset (or keep the one at `path`): copied from a preset, from another character,
or blank (Creator's default head and body), and opened for editing.

Re-running with the same path changes nothing (`changed: false`) unless `overwrite`. Exactly one of preset, source

ops.name: mh.add_item
ops.summary: Wear a wardrobe item: put it (a groom or garment from mh.wardrobe) in its slot of the character's collection
ops.doc:
Wear a wardrobe item: put it (a groom or garment from mh.wardrobe) in its slot of the character's collection
and select it there, replacing what the slot held; optionally set its parameters.

Args: character: the character. item: a wardrobe item path or asset name (WI_Hair_S_BuzzCut). slot: Hair,
Eyebrows, Beard, Mustache, Eyelashes, Peachfuzz, Outfits (guessed from the item's path when empty). params: the

Example: film-ue op mh.add_item character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava item=WI_Hair_L_Straight 'params={"Melanin": 1.0}'

ops.name: mh.apply
ops.summary: Converge a character to a `character` spec in one multi-tick job: make it (from a preset/source/blank), shape
ops.doc:
Converge a character to a `character` spec in one multi-tick job: make it (from a preset/source/blank), shape
the body and face, skin, eyes, eyelashes, teeth, makeup, grooms with colours, outfit, cloud rig and textures,
build the Blueprint, dress a placed actor. Every step is an mh.* op that changes only what differs, so a second
apply reports nothing changed.

Args: spec: the spec object (schema: character.schema.json; examples/unreal/character/). dry_run: return the
steps without running them. stop_before: an op name to stop at (e.g. "mh.rig" to shape without the cloud).
Returns: {"asset", "steps": [{"op", "args", "changed", "result"}], "changed", "describe"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.apply 'spec={"kind": "character", "version": 1, "name": "Ava", "asset": "/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava", "from": {"preset": "Ada"}, "body": {"Height": 168}}'

ops.name: mh.attach
ops.summary: Make a prop (an actor in the level) ride a bone of a placed MetaHuman, keeping where it is now: earrings on the
ops.doc:
Make a prop (an actor in the level) ride a bone of a placed MetaHuman, keeping where it is now: earrings on the
face's ear bones, a watch on the forearm. The prop is made Movable first (a Static root refuses to attach to a
moving bone without a word).

Args: label: the MetaHuman actor. prop: the prop's label. bone: the bone or socket (FACIAL_L_Ear4,
lowerarm_twist_02_l). component: Body or Face.
Returns: {"changed", "parent": component, "bone"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.attach label=Presenter prop=HerWatch bone=lowerarm_twist_02_l

ops.name: mh.auth_status
ops.summary: Whether the MetaHuman cloud services can sign in to Epic without asking.
ops.doc:
Whether the MetaHuman cloud services can sign in to Epic without asking.

Returns: {"signed_in": true|false|null (Windows: unknown, kept in the credential store), "credentials": n saved
EOS sign-ins on this machine, "platform"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.auth_status

ops.name: mh.body
ops.summary: Shape the parametric body by measurements: each named constraint becomes active at that value (None frees it).
ops.doc:
Shape the parametric body by measurements: each named constraint becomes active at that value (None frees it).

The engine hands the constraints out as copies: they are edited as copies and the whole list goes back in one
set_body_constraints, then commit_body_state (the operator's 'bodies via constraint copies' lesson). Names are
Creator's (Height, Chest, Waist, Hip, Across Shoulder, Neck, Bicep, Thigh, ...; mh.body_constraints lists them).
Args: character: the character asset. measurements: {name: cm or unitless, or None}. from_character: copy every
active constraint of another character first (its body; then `measurements` on top). reset: free every constraint
not named. save: save the asset.
Returns: {"body": {name: value or None}, "changed", "warnings"}. A body change after mh.rig needs a re-rig.
Example: film-ue op mh.body character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava 'measurements={"Height": 168, "Waist": 61}'

ops.doc:
The parametric body's measurement constraints: each one's current target, whether it is active and its range
(scaled with the height, as Creator shows them). Measurements are cm; Fat, Muscularity, Masculine/Feminine are
unitless.

Returns: {name: {"value", "active", "min", "max"}}.

ops.summary: The skeletal meshes of a built MetaHuman: its body and face (and skeletons), e.g. the target_mesh for
ops.doc:
The skeletal meshes of a built MetaHuman: its body and face (and skeletons), e.g. the target_mesh for

Give one of: label (a placed actor: read from its Body/Face components), bp (the built Blueprint: the meshes in
its unpack folder), character (the character asset: its last build, mh.build's bp).
Returns: {"body", "face", "body_skeleton", "face_skeleton"} package paths ("" when not found).

ops.name: mh.build
ops.summary: Assemble the character into a Blueprint (BP_<name>) with its face, body, grooms and outfit: what levels place.
ops.doc:
Assemble the character into a Blueprint (BP_<name>) with its face, body, grooms and outfit: what levels place.

Skips when the Blueprint exists and nothing that goes into it changed since it was built (`changed: false`);
`force` rebuilds. The engine call blocks the editor for the whole build (about 3 minutes for a cinematic build on
an L4) and cannot be split. The character must be rigged (mh.rig) and textured (mh.textures).
Args: character: the character. name (or bp_name, for callers whose own `name` argument is taken): the
Blueprint's name (BP_<name>) and unpack folder (default: the character's name without MH_). cinematic: legacy switch (False = optimized/high). pipeline: cinematic|optimized|uefn.
quality: low|medium|high|cinematic (LOD/detail level; optimized and uefn only, cinematic is always cinematic).
build_path: an absolute content folder for the built assets (default: the palette's unpack folder next to the
character, <folder>/Unpacked/<name>). common_path: where shared MetaHuman assets go. animation_system: e.g. AnimBP.
validate_wardrobe: run the wardrobe item checks. force: rebuild even if up to date.
Returns: {"bp", "changed", "seconds"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.build character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava name=Ava

ops.name: mh.can_build
ops.summary: Whether the character can be assembled now, and if not why and what to run.
ops.doc:
Whether the character can be assembled now, and if not why and what to run.

Returns: {"can_build", "why", "hint"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.can_build path=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava

ops.summary: Wear nothing in a slot (e.g. no Beard).

Wear nothing in a slot (e.g. no Beard).

Returns: {"slot", "changed"}.

ops.name: mh.clip_check
ops.summary: Does the body poke through a garment in the current pose? A numeric check (multi-tick): the posed body and
ops.doc:
Does the body poke through a garment in the current pose? A numeric check (multi-tick): the posed body and
garment are copied as meshes (Geometry Script, render LOD 0), and for body points under the garment (nearer than
near_cm) the signed distance to the garment's surface is measured; a point outside the garment by more than
tolerance_cm pokes through.

Needs the Geometry Script plugin. Scrub the sequence to the frame first (seq.stills / a pose) to check a pose.
Args: label: the MetaHuman actor. garment: its garment component. samples: body points checked (spread evenly).
max_poke_fraction: the share of checked points allowed through.
Returns: {"pass", "metric": poke fraction, "threshold", "why", "checked", "pokes", "max_cm", "worst": [[x, y, z,
cm], ...]}.
Example: film-ue op mh.clip_check label=Presenter garment=Top

ops.name: mh.cloth_inflate
ops.summary: Push a garment out along its normals by `cm`, so skin under tight cloth stops poking through. A multi-tick job.
ops.doc:
Push a garment out along its normals by `cm`, so skin under tight cloth stops poking through. A multi-tick job.

Nothing the renderer is drawing is ever edited: a material in use that is reparented or recompiled while frames
render trips `UniformExpressionCache... == Material.GetRenderingThreadShaderMap()` and takes the editor down (it
did, right after a MetaHuman rebuild had made fresh garment instances). So the worn instance is copied to
`{folder}/{label}_<name>_Inflate`, the copy is parented on project copies of its plugin chain whose master gains a
World Position Offset (normal x FM_Inflate), every shader finishes compiling, the editor ticks a few frames, and
only then does the component swap to the copy. A master already in use is never recompiled (a new one is made);
re-running on an inflated garment only changes the amount, a plain parameter change that is safe. `which` limits it
to the garments whose material name contains it (e.g. "Shirt": a top pushed out over shorts that stay put, else
both move together and the shorts' waistband still shows through the tee); others already inflated go back to 0.

Returns: {material name: amount or [copies made]}.
Example: film-ue op mh.cloth_inflate label=Presenter cm=1.0 which=Shirt

ops.summary: An assembled MetaHuman actor's skeletal mesh components: mesh, animation mode and class.

A character's whole state as JSON: what the `character` spec planner diffs against.

The eyelashes (part of the head model): type (None, ShortSparse, ShortFine, ShortThin, LongSlightCurl,

ops.summary: The eyes: iris (pattern Iris001..Iris009, colour as palette u/v, blend, limbal ring), pupil, cornea, sclera,
ops.doc:
The eyes: iris (pattern Iris001..Iris009, colour as palette u/v, blend, limbal ring), pupil, cornea, sclera,
for both eyes or each.

Args: path: the character. both/left/right: FMetaHumanCharacterEyeProperties fields as nested JSON, e.g.
{"iris": {"pattern": "Iris003", "primary_color_u": 0.2, "primary_color_v": 0.6}, "sclera": {"vascularity_intensity": 0.5}}.
`left`/`right` go over `both`. Returns: {"changed", "eyes_settings"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.eyes path=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava 'both={"iris": {"primary_color_u": 0.2}}'

ops.name: mh.face
ops.summary: Shape the face: blend presets or other characters' faces, set the face model's coefficients, or move face
ops.doc:
Shape the face: blend presets or other characters' faces, set the face model's coefficients, or move face
landmarks (Creator's sculpt points).

blend mixes the face model coefficients of the sources by weight (normalised to sum 1): Creator's own blend tool
is not exposed to Python, this is its linear equivalent on the model (experimental: judge the still). landmarks
moves points by deltas in cm ({index: [dx, dy, dz]}; mh.face_landmarks lists them). A face change on a rigged
character removes the rig first (`unrig`), as Creator does: re-run mh.rig, mh.textures, mh.build.
Landmark moves are deltas: what was applied is fingerprinted on the asset (mh.describe face.applied), so the same
call twice moves them once; `force` applies again.
Args: path: the character. blend: {preset name or character path: weight}. coefficients: the full list (from
mh.describe full=true). landmarks: {index: [dx, dy, dz]} cm. unrig: allow removing the rig. force: apply even if
this exact face was applied last. save: save the asset.
Returns: {"changed", "coefficients": n, "max_delta", "unrigged"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.face path=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava 'blend={"Ada": 0.7, "Vivian": 0.3}'

ops.name: mh.face_landmarks
ops.summary: The face's landmark positions (Creator's sculpt points), for mh.face landmarks={index: [dx, dy, dz]}.
ops.doc:
The face's landmark positions (Creator's sculpt points), for mh.face landmarks={index: [dx, dy, dz]}.

Returns: {"count", "landmarks": [[x, y, z] cm, ...]} in the face mesh's space.
Example: film-ue op mh.face_landmarks path=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava

ops.name: mh.find
ops.summary: The MetaHuman character assets under a folder, with whether each is rigged/textured and its built Blueprint.
ops.doc:
The MetaHuman character assets under a folder, with whether each is rigged/textured and its built Blueprint.

Returns: [{"path", "rigged", "has_high_res_textures", "bp"}].
Example: film-ue op mh.find folder=/Game/Characters

ops.name: mh.from_preset
ops.summary: A new character asset copied from a preset (e.g. 'Trey'), opened for editing (legacy form of mh.add).
ops.doc:
A new character asset copied from a preset (e.g. 'Trey'), opened for editing (legacy form of mh.add).

Args: preset: a name from mh.presets (or a character path to copy). dest: the new asset's path. overwrite: replace
what is at dest. Returns: dest.
Example: film-ue op mh.from_preset preset=Ada dest=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava

ops.name: mh.garment
ops.summary: Set parameters on a worn garment's material (slots whose name contains `which`): `vectors` take linear [r,g,b],
ops.doc:
Set parameters on a worn garment's material (slots whose name contains `which`): `vectors` take linear [r,g,b],
e.g. the default garment's {"diffuse_color_1": [...], "diffuse_color_2": [...]} is its colour.

Returns: {material instance: [parameters set]}.
Example: film-ue op mh.garment label=Presenter which=Shirt 'vectors={"diffuse_color_1": [0.2, 0.3, 0.2]}'

ops.name: mh.groom
ops.summary: A groom in one call: wear `item` in `slot` (or keep what is worn, or wear nothing with item="none") and set its
ops.doc:
A groom in one call: wear `item` in `slot` (or keep what is worn, or wear nothing with item="none") and set its
colour (melanin: 0 blond .. 1 black; redness 0..1) and any other groom parameter.

Args: slot: Hair|Eyebrows|Beard|Mustache|Eyelashes|Peachfuzz. item: a groom wardrobe item (mh.wardrobe kind=Hair),
"" to keep, "none" to clear. Returns: {"slot", "item", "changed", "params"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.groom character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava slot=Hair item=WI_Hair_L_Straight melanin=1.0 redness=0.05

ops.name: mh.import_garment
ops.summary: Import a garment FBX (authored in cm, skinned to the MetaHuman body skeleton) as a skeletal mesh on that
ops.doc:
Import a garment FBX (authored in cm, skinned to the MetaHuman body skeleton) as a skeletal mesh on that
skeleton, for mh.dress. Checks the units: a garment that comes in tiny or huge (metres vs cm) is an error.

Args: fbx: the file on the box (absolute path). dest: the asset path (/Game/Outfits/Ava/SKM_Ava_Top).
skeleton: the skeleton asset (default the MetaHuman body skeleton). replace: re-import over an existing one.
Returns: {"path", "changed", "bounds_cm": [x, y, z] half sizes, "slots": [material slot names]}.
Example: film-ue op mh.import_garment fbx=/srv/proj/Saved/Import/her_top.fbx dest=/Game/Outfits/Ava/SKM_Ava_Top

ops.name: mh.item_params
ops.summary: The instance parameters of the item worn in a slot, with their values: for a groom Melanin, Redness,
ops.doc:
The instance parameters of the item worn in a slot, with their values: for a groom Melanin, Redness,
Roughness, Whiteness, Lightness, DyeColor, bUseOmbre/OmbreU/OmbreV/..., bUseRegions/..., bUseHighlights/...
(MetaHumanDefaultGroomPipeline); for a garment its material colours.

Returns: {"slot", "item", "params": {name: value}}.
Example: film-ue op mh.item_params character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava slot=Hair

ops.name: mh.item_set
ops.summary: Set instance parameters of the item worn in a slot: hair colour by melanin/redness (0..1), dye colour, ombre,
ops.doc:
Set instance parameters of the item worn in a slot: hair colour by melanin/redness (0..1), dye colour, ombre,
highlights; a garment's colours. Only differing values are written.

Returns: {"slot", "changed", "params"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.item_set character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava slot=Hair 'params={"Melanin": 1.0, "Redness": 0.05}'

ops.name: mh.leader
ops.summary: Put every garment of a placed MetaHuman back on leader pose to its body, in one pass (a garment that lost it
ops.doc:
Put every garment of a placed MetaHuman back on leader pose to its body, in one pass (a garment that lost it
stays in its bind pose while the body moves). Run it after any change to the actor's components, after a level
load, and before rendering.

Returns: {"garments": {name: {"leader", "bone_gap_cm", "ok"}}, "ok", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.leader label=Presenter

ops.name: mh.leader_check
ops.summary: Whether every garment follows the body: a verdict for QA. Each garment must lead from the body and sit on the
ops.doc:
Whether every garment follows the body: a verdict for QA. Each garment must lead from the body and sit on the
body's bones (the largest gap over pelvis, spine, head, hands, calves under 0.1 cm).

Returns: {"pass", "metric": worst bone gap cm, "threshold": 0.1, "why", "garments"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.leader_check label=Presenter

ops.name: mh.login
ops.summary: Start Epic's sign-in for the MetaHuman cloud services if there is none, and return at once.
ops.doc:
Start Epic's sign-in for the MetaHuman cloud services if there is none, and return at once.

With `exchange_code` (a one-time code from Epic's account service, valid ~5 minutes) the next cloud request signs
in with it, no browser (the code is set in the CVar MetaHuman.Cloud.Config.ExchangeCode; the console echoes it to
the log, so use a fresh single-use code). Without it, a rig is requested on a throwaway character so the service
starts its device sign-in: the engine hands the page to the system browser, which on a box without a desktop
keeps it for `film-ue epic-login`. The sign-in then persists across editor restarts.
Returns: {"signed_in", "requested", "exchange_code_set"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.login

ops.name: mh.makeup
ops.summary: Makeup: foundation (apply, colour, intensity, concealer), eyes (None, ThinLiner, SoftSmokey, FullThinLiner,
ops.doc:
Makeup: foundation (apply, colour, intensity, concealer), eyes (None, ThinLiner, SoftSmokey, FullThinLiner,
CatEye, PandaSmudge, DramaticSmudge, DoubleMod, ClassicBar), blush (None, Angled, Apple, LowSweep, HighCurve), lips
(None, Natural, Hollywood, Cupid), each with colours, roughness, opacity.

Args: settings: FMetaHumanCharacterMakeupSettings fields, e.g. {"lips": {"type": "Natural", "color": [0.3, 0.05,
0.05]}, "eyes": {"type": "ThinLiner"}}. Returns: {"changed", "makeup_settings"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.makeup path=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava 'settings={"lips": {"type": "Natural"}}'

ops.name: mh.palette
ops.summary: What the character wears now: its collection's slots, every item in its palette and the selection per slot
ops.doc:
What the character wears now: its collection's slots, every item in its palette and the selection per slot
with the selected items' parameters.

Returns: {"slots": [...], "items": [...], "selected": {slot: {"item", "params"} or null}}.
Example: film-ue op mh.palette character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava

ops.name: mh.presets
ops.summary: The preset characters MetaHuman Creator ships (needs the engine's Creator Core Data).
ops.doc:
The preset characters MetaHuman Creator ships (needs the engine's Creator Core Data).

Returns: preset names, e.g. ["Ada", "Jorge", ...], for mh.add preset=<name>.
Example: film-ue op mh.presets

ops.name: mh.preview
ops.summary: A live MetaHuman Editor actor of the character in the open level, with no rig and no build: it follows
ops.doc:
A live MetaHuman Editor actor of the character in the open level, with no rig and no build: it follows
changes made to the character (body, face, skin, wardrobe), for stills while shaping one.

Re-running with the same label moves the existing one. Args: label: the actor label (default MHPreview_<name>).
loc: [x, y, z] cm. yaw_deg: facing. transient: not saved with the level.
Returns: {"label", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.preview path=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava 'loc=[0,0,0]'

ops.name: mh.remove
ops.summary: Delete a character asset (and with `built`, the Blueprint mh.build made from it). Removing nothing is fine.
ops.doc:
Delete a character asset (and with `built`, the Blueprint mh.build made from it). Removing nothing is fine.

Returns: {"removed": [paths], "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.remove path=/Game/_Selftest/mh/MH_Scratch built=true

ops.name: mh.rig
ops.summary: Epic's cloud auto-rig, as a multi-tick job (about 30 s once signed in). Needed before mh.textures and
ops.doc:
Epic's cloud auto-rig, as a multi-tick job (about 30 s once signed in). Needed before mh.textures and
mh.build, and again after any body or face change.

Skips the request when the character is rigged and its body and face are what they were at the last rig
(`changed: false`); `force` re-rigs anyway. Without a saved Epic sign-in it fails at once (require_login) instead
of waiting on a browser.
Args: character: the character. full: joints + blend shapes (what facial animation needs) or joints only.
timeout_s: give up after. force: rig even if up to date. require_login: fail fast without a sign-in.
Returns: {"changed", "seconds", "rig": "full"|"joints", "log"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.rig character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava

ops.name: mh.settings_fields
ops.summary: The fields (and current values) of one of a character's settings, for writing a spec or an mh.* call.
ops.doc:
The fields (and current values) of one of a character's settings, for writing a spec or an mh.* call.

Args: which: skin|eyes|makeup|eyelashes|teeth. Returns: the settings as nested JSON with their current values.
Example: film-ue op mh.settings_fields path=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava which=makeup

ops.name: mh.skin
ops.summary: The skin: tone (Creator's palette coordinates u, v), roughness, and any other skin setting (freckles, accents
ops.doc:
The skin: tone (Creator's palette coordinates u, v), roughness, and any other skin setting (freckles, accents
by face region, palms, nails, body/face texture variants, the texture resolutions the cloud makes).

Committing skin settings discards the character's high-resolution textures (the engine's rule), so this commits
only when something differs; after a change, run mh.textures again before mh.build.
Args: character: the character. u, v: tone 0..1. roughness: 0.85..1.15. settings: FMetaHumanCharacterSkinSettings
fields as nested JSON, e.g. {"freckles": {"density": 0.6, "mask": "Type1"}, "accents": {"cheeks": {"redness":
0.7}}, "skin": {"face_texture_index": 1}}. texture_resolution: 2k|4k|8k for every texture mh.textures fetches.
Returns: {"changed", "u", "v", "roughness", "skin_settings": {...}}.
Example: film-ue op mh.skin character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava u=0.55 v=0.45 'settings={"freckles": {"density": 0.3}}'

ops.name: mh.teeth
ops.summary: The teeth (part of the head model): length, spacing, upper/lower shift, overbite, overjet, worn down,
ops.doc:
The teeth (part of the head model): length, spacing, upper/lower shift, overbite, overjet, worn down,
polycanine, receding gums, narrowness, variation (each -1..1 or 0..1), teeth/gum/plaque colours, plaque amount.

Args: settings: FMetaHumanCharacterTeethProperties fields, e.g. {"tooth_length": 0.2, "teeth_color": [0.9, 0.88, 0.8]}.
Returns: {"changed", "teeth"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.teeth path=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava 'settings={"overbite": 0.3}'

ops.name: mh.textures
ops.summary: Epic's cloud high-resolution skin texture sources (face and body), as a multi-tick job (about 20 s). Needs a
ops.doc:
Epic's cloud high-resolution skin texture sources (face and body), as a multi-tick job (about 20 s). Needs a
rig first (the service signs in during the rig); mh.build needs them.

Skips when the character already has them (`changed: false`); a skin change (mh.skin) discards them. The
resolution is the skin setting desired_texture_sources_resolutions (mh.skin texture_resolution=4k).
Returns: {"changed", "seconds", "has_high_res_textures", "log"}.
Example: film-ue op mh.textures character=/Game/Characters/Ava/MH_Ava

ops.name: mh.variants
ops.summary: N distinct, plausible characters from one seed and ranges (age band, sex, height, build, skin tone, hair and
ops.doc:
N distinct, plausible characters from one seed and ranges (age band, sex, height, build, skin tone, hair and
wardrobe pools): deterministic per seed, as `character` specs; with `make`, each one is made and converged by
mh.apply (a multi-tick job).

Args: cast: the cast object (kind cast: seed, count, folder, presets, ranges; schema cast.schema.json).
make: create/converge every member (needs the Epic sign-in unless rig is none or stop_before="mh.rig").
stop_before: passed to each mh.apply (e.g. "mh.rig": shape only). preview: also place a live preview of each
member in a row along +Y (labels Preview_<name>), for stills and a contact sheet. spacing_cm: the row spacing.
Returns: {"members": [specs], "traits", "distances": nearest earlier member, "changed", "made": [{"name",
"changed"}], "previews": [labels]}.
Example: film-ue op mh.variants 'cast={"seed": 7, "count": 6, "folder": "/Game/Extras", "presets": ["Ada", "Jorge"], "rig": "none"}'

ops.name: mh.wardrobe
ops.summary: Wardrobe items (grooms and clothing) the engine ships: kind Hair, Beards, Eyebrows, Eyelashes, Mustaches,
ops.doc:
Wardrobe items (grooms and clothing) the engine ships: kind Hair, Beards, Eyebrows, Eyelashes, Mustaches,
Peachfuzz, Clothing, or empty for all.

Returns: item asset paths for mh.add_item / mh.groom.
Example: film-ue op mh.wardrobe kind=Hair

ops.name: ops.broken
ops.summary: The op modules that failed to import, with their full tracebacks ({} when all loaded).
ops.doc: The op modules that failed to import, with their full tracebacks ({} when all loaded).

ops.name: ops.schema
ops.summary: Every op's signature, docstring and flags as JSON, for generating a CLI or SDK and for discovery:
ops.doc:
Every op's signature, docstring and flags as JSON, for generating a CLI or SDK and for discovery:
{"version": 1, "ops": [{"name", "area", "verb", "params": [{"name", "type", "required", "default"}], ...}],
"broken": {module: error}}. Example: film-ue op ops.schema prefix=seq.

ops.name: perf.analyze_audio
ops.summary: A voice file's timing for a performance, with no engine work: duration, stressed syllables (emphasis: beat
ops.doc:
A voice file's timing for a performance, with no engine work: duration, stressed syllables (emphasis: beat
nods and brow flashes land there), pauses and phrase ends (blinks), and a 25 Hz loudness envelope.

Args: wav: a PCM WAV path on the editor's machine. top: keep only the strongest n emphases (0 = all).
Returns: {"duration_s", "emphasis": [[t, strength]], "pauses": [[t0, t1]], "phrase_ends": [t], "talking":
[[t0, t1]], "envelope": {"rate": 25, "values": [...]}}.
Example: film-ue op perf.analyze_audio wav=/home/ue/Audio/line1.wav

ops.name: perf.apply
ops.summary: Converge the editor on a PERFORMANCE spec (kind: performance): speech-solve the lines whose audio or mood
ops.doc:
Converge the editor on a PERFORMANCE spec (kind: performance): speech-solve the lines whose audio or mood
changed, compose the face, key the body and the actor's moves in the sequence; re-run safely (a converged spec
does nothing). `dry_run` returns the plan only. A multi-tick job (speech solves take seconds per line).

Returns: {"converged", "rounds", "ran": [{"op", "why", "result"}], "report": the face's naturalness checks}.
Example: film-ue op perf.apply spec=@films/demo/perf/intro.yaml

ops.name: perf.calibrate
ops.summary: Measure, on the real rig, which way HeadYaw/HeadPitch/HeadRoll turn the head and how far eyeLook* turns the
ops.doc:
Measure, on the real rig, which way HeadYaw/HeadPitch/HeadRoll turn the head and how far eyeLook* turns the
eyes, and save it for this face skeleton (Saved/fmbridge/perf/signs_<skeleton>.json): perf.face and perf.apply
then use it. Plays a scratch animation on the actor's face in a scratch sequence and samples the eye bones.
Run once per face skeleton (the face must be driven by Sequencer: mh.drive_face). A multi-tick job, ~20 s.

Returns: {"signs": {"yaw", "pitch", "roll", "eye_deg", "eye_flip", "measured"}, "file", "raw": {...}}.
Example: film-ue op perf.calibrate label=Presenter

ops.name: perf.calibrate_body
ops.summary: Measure, on the real body skeleton, which local axis (and sign) of each spine, clavicle and pelvis bone bends the
ops.doc:
Measure, on the real body skeleton, which local axis (and sign) of each spine, clavicle and pelvis bone bends the
body forward (flex), to the character's left (side; for a clavicle: lifts it) and turns it left (twist), and which
of the pelvis's parent axes shifts it to the left; with the bones' rest pose. Saved per skeleton
(Saved/fmbridge/perf/body_<skeleton>.json) for anim.body_life. Plays scratch animations on the actor's body in a
scratch sequence and samples the head, clavicles, upper arms and feet ("forward" is where the feet point).
A multi-tick job, ~1 min.

Returns: {"skeleton", "axes": {bone: {"flex": [axis, sign], "side": [...], "twist": [...]}}, "shift_axis",
"file", "raw"}.
Example: film-ue op perf.calibrate_body label=Presenter

ops.name: perf.check
ops.summary: Will this face read as alive? Same as anim.check (naturalness numbers with pass/fail and why).
ops.doc:
Will this face read as alive? Same as anim.check (naturalness numbers with pass/fail and why).
Example: film-ue op perf.check anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1_perf

ops.name: perf.compose
ops.summary: Compose a performance spec into the sequence: one continuous face animation (every line's lip-sync placed at
ops.doc:
Compose a performance spec into the sequence: one continuous face animation (every line's lip-sync placed at
its time, with the head, eyes, blinks, moods and expressions of perfkit over the whole timeline, so nothing
jumps between lines) on the face track, the body's idle/gesture/walk sections, and the actor's transform keys.
perf.apply calls it after the speech solves; call it yourself to re-key without re-solving.
Returns: {"face_anim", "fingerprint", "frames", "report", "timeline", "body_sections", "notes", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op perf.compose spec=@examples/unreal/performance/listener.yaml

ops.name: perf.describe
ops.summary: An actor's performance in a sequence: the animation sections on its face and body tracks, the face
ops.doc:
An actor's performance in a sequence: the animation sections on its face and body tracks, the face
animation's perf metadata (which spec, its fingerprint), and its transform keys.
Example: film-ue op perf.describe sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 label=Presenter

ops.name: perf.face
ops.summary: Make a face animation (a speech solve, or any MetaHuman face animation) read as alive: write a copy whose head
ops.doc:
Make a face animation (a speech solve, or any MetaHuman face animation) read as alive: write a copy whose head
turns follow the gaze (eyes lead, the head eases with overshoot and settles), with nods and brow flashes on the
stressed words, irregular asymmetric blinks (with big gaze shifts and at phrase ends), fixational eye darts, a
mood's baseline expression, and micro-motion in every hold; the solver's own head motion is softened under it
and the lip-sync is kept.

Args (times in seconds from the animation's start, angles in degrees in the CHARACTER's frame: yaw + = their
left, pitch + = up):
  anim: the source animation. out: where to write (default <anim>_perf); re-written on each call.
  wav: the line's audio, for automatic emphasis and phrase ends (perf.analyze_audio).
  gaze: shifts [{"t", "yaw", "pitch", "scan": face|lens|still, "dist_cm", "head": share 0..1}]; default: hold
  straight ahead on a lens. start_gaze: [yaw, pitch] at t=0. lead: eyes|head.
  head: style {"gain", "rest_roll_deg", "rest_pitch_deg", "micro_deg", "breath_deg", "lean", "speech_gain"}.
  nods: [{"t", "kind": yes|beat|up|no, "depth_deg", "count"}]. tilts: [{"t", "until", "roll_deg"}].
  mood: one mood over the whole clip, or moods: [{"t0", "t1", "mood", "intensity"}] (perf.vocab lists them).
  expressions: [{"preset", "t", "until", "intensity", "asym"}]. emphasis: [[t, strength]] or "auto" (from wav).
  layers: subset of head, eyes, blinks, expressions, brows, nods. solver_head: soften|keep|replace.
  blink_mode: replace|keep|max. blink_state: talk|listen|rest|focus|nervous|calm. energy: >1 brisker head.
  mouth_mix: smile strength on a talking mouth (0..1). signs: rig signs (default perf.calibrate's, else guesses).
  plot: a PNG path on the box: the result's curves drawn as strips (perf.plot) to look at.
Returns: {"out", "changed", "plan": {shifts, nods, blinks, expressions, ...}, "report": naturalness checks,
"curves": n, "plot"?: {"path", "width", "height"}}.
Example: film-ue op perf.face anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_line1 wav=/home/ue/Audio/line1.wav mood=warm 'gaze=[{"t":0,"yaw":0,"scan":"lens"},{"t":2.5,"yaw":25,"pitch":-5}]'

ops.name: perf.gestures
ops.summary: Gestures timed to their beats: each {"anim" | "name", "at_s" (the beat: the stressed word), "stroke_s" (where
ops.doc:
Gestures timed to their beats: each {"anim" | "name", "at_s" (the beat: the stressed word), "stroke_s" (where
the stroke falls in the clip; default 40% in), "hold_s", "intensity"}; the clip starts so its stroke lands
`lead_s` before the beat. Overlaps are moved or dropped (see notes). Adds the sections to the body track.
Example: film-ue op perf.gestures sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 label=Presenter 'gestures=[{"anim":"/Game/Anim/AS_OpenPalms","at_s":2.1,"stroke_s":0.7}]'

ops.name: perf.head_curves
ops.summary: Preview organic head motion with no engine and no animation: the HeadYaw/Pitch/Roll curves (character frame,
ops.doc:
Preview organic head motion with no engine and no animation: the HeadYaw/Pitch/Roll curves (character frame,
degrees) perfkit makes for these gaze shifts, nods and tilts, with the plan and the head checks. For trying
styles before writing them (perf.face).
Example: film-ue op perf.head_curves duration_s=6 'gaze=[{"t":1,"yaw":30},{"t":3.5,"yaw":-10,"pitch":-5}]' 'nods=[{"t":4.5,"kind":"nod"}]'

ops.name: perf.idle
ops.summary: An idle that never loops visibly on an actor's body track: segments of 4-9 s from the given idle clips at
ops.doc:
An idle that never loops visibly on an actor's body track: segments of 4-9 s from the given idle clips at
random offsets and play rates 0.92-1.08, cross-fading into each other; split around `gaps` [[start, end]]
frames (where gestures play). end 0 = the sequence's end.
Example: film-ue op perf.idle sequence=/Game/Shots/S010 label=Presenter 'clips=["/MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Animation/TemplateAnimations/Technical_Loops/Idle/mhc_mh001_fmn_b_idle"]'

ops.name: perf.lock_eyes
ops.summary: Measured eye contact with the spec's camera over the composed face (anim.gaze_lock: the eye curves solved
ops.doc:
Measured eye contact with the spec's camera over the composed face (anim.gaze_lock: the eye curves solved
from the eye bones' real pose on the lines that look at the camera). A multi-tick job.
Example: film-ue op perf.lock_eyes spec=@examples/unreal/performance/presenter_intro.yaml

ops.name: perf.plan
ops.summary: What perf.apply would do for a performance spec, without doing it: {"steps": [{"op", "args", "why"}],
ops.doc:
What perf.apply would do for a performance spec, without doing it: {"steps": [{"op", "args", "why"}],
"compiled": timeline, body sections and notes}. Empty steps = converged.
Example: film-ue op perf.plan spec=@performance.yaml

ops.name: perf.plot
ops.summary: Draw a face animation's performance as a PNG (head yaw/pitch/roll, the left eye in the head, blinks, upper
ops.doc:
Draw a face animation's performance as a PNG (head yaw/pitch/roll, the left eye in the head, blinks, upper
face, mouth, on one time axis): look at it to judge motion without rendering. Straight ramps and flat holds in the
head strip are robotic; eased S-curves with a small overshoot and a slight wobble are alive.

Args: anim: a face AnimSequence. out: PNG path on the box. signs: rig signs (default the calibration).
t0_s/t1_s: the time window (default the whole animation).
Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "changed": true}.
Example: film-ue op perf.plot anim=/Game/Speech/Anim/AS_l1_perf out=/tmp/l1_perf.png

ops.name: perf.solve
ops.summary: A line's speech solve (speech.to_face) tagged with the key of what it was made from, so perf.plan knows when
ops.doc:
A line's speech solve (speech.to_face) tagged with the key of what it was made from, so perf.plan knows when
it is up to date. A multi-tick job.
Example: film-ue op perf.solve wav=/home/ue/Audio/l1.wav name=intro_l1 face_mesh=/Game/MetaHumans/Ada/Face/Ada_FaceMesh mood=HAPPINESS

ops.name: perf.state
ops.summary: What a performance spec depends on, read from the editor (the planner's input): the sequence's rate, the
ops.doc:
What a performance spec depends on, read from the editor (the planner's input): the sequence's rate, the
actor's position/facing/head height and face mesh, every target's position, clip lengths, each line's audio
analysis and speech-solve key, and the composed face animation's fingerprint.
Example: film-ue op perf.state spec=@performance.yaml

ops.name: perf.turn_to
ops.summary: Turn an actor in place to face a target (a point, an actor, "Label:Component:bone") or a yaw (degrees),
ops.doc:
Turn an actor in place to face a target (a point, an actor, "Label:Component:bone") or a yaw (degrees),
eased with a skewed min-jerk over 0.45 s + 0.5 s per 90 deg (/ speed); keys its transform (replacing the
transform track, so give a whole route to perf.walk_to or a spec instead when there are several moves).
Example: film-ue op perf.turn_to sequence=/Game/Shots/S020 label=Presenter target=Guest at_frame=48

ops.name: perf.vocab
ops.summary: The words a performance understands: expression presets (with their curves), moods (and the speech solver
ops.doc:
The words a performance understands: expression presets (with their curves), moods (and the speech solver
mood each maps to), nod kinds, face layers, blink states, gaze scan modes.
Example: film-ue op perf.vocab

ops.name: perf.walk_to
ops.summary: Walk an actor to a point in a sequence: turn in place if needed, accelerate, follow `path` waypoints, brake,
ops.doc:
Walk an actor to a point in a sequence: turn in place if needed, accelerate, follow `path` waypoints, brake,
optionally turn to face `end_facing`; the actor's transform is keyed (replacing its transform track) and the walk
loop is added on the body track at the play rate that matches its own speed (`clip_speed_cm_s`, default
speed_cm_s: rate 1).

Args: to: [x, y, z] cm, or a target (actor label, "Label:Component:bone"). at_frame: when it sets off.
speed_cm_s: cruise speed (people: 110-150). facing_offset_deg: the actor's forward vs its mesh's (MetaHumans: 0).
Returns: {"changed", "keys", "frames": [start, stop], "distance_cm", "walk": the walk section, "slide": check}.
Example: film-ue op perf.walk_to sequence=/Game/Shots/S020 label=Presenter 'to=[300,120,0]' walk_anim=/MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Animation/UEFNAnimPreset/Locomotion/AS_MH_Neutral_Walk_Loop_F at_frame=24

ops.name: pose.apply
ops.summary: Pose a character at a frame of a sequence: key its Control Rig so each effector reaches the pose's goal, solved
ops.doc:
Pose a character at a frame of a sequence: key its Control Rig so each effector reaches the pose's goal, solved
closed-loop on what the engine evaluates, then report the remaining error per effector.

Args: label: the character (its body's skeletal mesh; `component` names it, else the one with a pelvis).
pose: a library name (pose.library) or {effector: {"anchor", "offset": [fwd, right, up]} | "keep" | [x,y,z]}.
params: {"drop_cm": 45} for sit. rig_class: the body's Control Rig Blueprint, to make the rig track if missing.
controls: {effector: control name} overrides for the pattern match. tolerance_cm, iterations: the solve.
Goals are relative to the character's REST pose, captured the first time a pose is applied in this sequence
(stored on it); `reset_rest` captures it again (after the character moved).
A multi-tick job. Re-running converges (the controls are re-solved to the same goals).
Returns: {"pass", "errors_cm": {effector: cm}, "controls": {effector: control}, "iterations", "goals",
"issues", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op pose.apply label=Host sequence=/Game/Seq/S010 frame=48 pose=hands_on_hips

ops.name: pose.check
ops.summary: Is the character in the pose at that frame? Scrub there and measure each effector against the pose's goals.
ops.doc:
Is the character in the pose at that frame? Scrub there and measure each effector against the pose's goals.
Goals are anchored on the rest pose pose.apply stored on the sequence, else on the bones now (a held pose then
checks against itself); `rest` ({bone: [x, y, z]}) overrides both. A multi-tick job.

Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"errors_cm"}}.
Example: film-ue op pose.check label=Host sequence=/Game/Seq/S010 frame=60 pose=hands_on_hips

ops.name: pose.library
ops.summary: The named poses: what each looks like and which effectors it sets (hand_l/r, foot_l/r, pelvis, chest, head),
ops.doc:
The named poses: what each looks like and which effectors it sets (hand_l/r, foot_l/r, pelvis, chest, head),
with the goal table (anchor + [forward, right, up] cm in the body's frame) for one `pose`.

Example: film-ue op pose.library pose=hands_on_hips

ops.name: qa.baseline_check
ops.summary: What a test does per still: compare with the baseline, or make it the baseline when there is none.
ops.doc:
What a test does per still: compare with the baseline, or make it the baseline when there is none.

Args: suite/name/image: as qa.baseline_compare. mode: auto (compare, or create when missing), compare (never
create), update (replace: accept the new look), off. diff_out: heatmap when it differs. meta: stored on create.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"status": created|updated|match|differs|different|no_baseline|off, ...}}.
Example: film-ue op qa.baseline_check suite=selftest/look name=key image=/srv/st/look_key.png

ops.name: qa.baseline_compare
ops.summary: A still against its baseline: SSIM, PSNR, changed cells, exposure shift, a diff heatmap when it moved.
ops.doc:
A still against its baseline: SSIM, PSNR, changed cells, exposure shift, a diff heatmap when it moved.

Args: suite/name: the baseline. image: the new still (PNG on the box). diff_out: write the heatmap there when it
differs. min_ssim: override the match threshold (default the baseline's own, else 0.95).
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"status": match|differs|different|no_baseline, "ssim", "psnr",
"changed", "stops_shift", "mean_shift", "diff"?}}. no_baseline passes (with an info issue).
Example: film-ue op qa.baseline_compare suite=film/s010 name=00048 image=/srv/qa/new/00048.png diff_out=/srv/qa/d.png

ops.name: qa.baseline_list
ops.summary: The baselines on the box (all, or one suite and its sub-suites).
ops.doc:
The baselines on the box (all, or one suite and its sub-suites).

Returns: {"root", "baselines": [{"suite", "name", "updated", "size", "png", "json", "rel"}]}; `rel` is the PNG's
path under root (film-qa baseline pull mirrors it).
Example: film-ue op qa.baseline_list suite=selftest

ops.name: qa.baseline_remove
ops.summary: Delete one baseline (nothing there is fine).
ops.doc:
Delete one baseline (nothing there is fine).

Returns: {"changed": bool}.
Example: film-ue op qa.baseline_remove suite=film/s010 name=00048

ops.name: qa.baseline_save
ops.summary: Keep a still as the golden baseline suite/name (with its exposure/colour numbers).
ops.doc:
Keep a still as the golden baseline suite/name (with its exposure/colour numbers).

Args: suite: a group ("selftest/look", "film/s010"; slashes make folders). name: the still's name in it.
image: PNG path on the box. overwrite: replace an existing baseline (accept a change); otherwise an existing one
is kept. meta: anything to remember (camera, frame, commit). min_ssim: this baseline's own match threshold (a
noisy shot).
Returns: {"suite", "name", "png", "json", "size", "metrics", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op qa.baseline_save suite=film/s010 name=00048 image=/srv/qa/s010/00048.png

ops.name: qa.compare
ops.summary: A PNG against a reference PNG: SSIM, PSNR, which cells changed, mean colour shift, and a diff heatmap.
ops.doc:
A PNG against a reference PNG: SSIM, PSNR, which cells changed, mean colour shift, and a diff heatmap.

Args: image, reference: PNG paths (same aspect; sizes may differ). out_diff: write the heatmap there ("" skips).
min_ssim: below this the check fails/warns. width_px: compare size. grid: [cols, rows] for the change map.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"ssim", "psnr", "grid", "changed", "mean_shift", "verdict"},
"diff"?: path}.
Example: film-ue op qa.compare image=/tmp/qa/new/00048.png reference=/tmp/qa/ref/00048.png out_diff=/tmp/qa/d.png

ops.name: qa.diff
ops.summary: What changed between two snapshots (files from qa.snapshot), or between one and the level now.
ops.doc:
What changed between two snapshots (files from qa.snapshot), or between one and the level now.

Args: before: snapshot path. after: snapshot path ("" = now). ignore: labels or prefixes ("Light*") to skip.
severity: "info" when versions are expected to differ, "warn" when they should match. tolerance: {"loc_cm",
"rot_deg", "scale", "prop"}.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"added", "removed", "changed", "summary"}}.
Example: film-ue op qa.diff before=/tmp/qa/before.json 'ignore=["FMQA_*"]'

ops.name: qa.exposure
ops.summary: Exposure of a PNG: histogram, luma mean/median/percentiles, clipped and crushed %, stops from mid grey, per
ops.doc:
Exposure of a PNG: histogram, luma mean/median/percentiles, clipped and crushed %, stops from mid grey, per
region, and a verdict against a target range.

Args: image: PNG path. target_stops: [lo, hi] the mean should land in (stops from 18% grey; default -2.5..+1.5).
regions: {name: [x0,y0,x1,y1]} (0..1) measured separately, e.g. a face box from qa.framing.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"exposure", "histogram" (32 bins of luma), "regions"}}.
Example: film-ue op qa.exposure image=/tmp/qa/a.png 'target_stops=[-2,-0.5]'

ops.name: qa.floating
ops.summary: Actors hovering above the surface under them: a line trace down from the bottom of each one's bounds (its
ops.doc:
Actors hovering above the surface under them: a line trace down from the bottom of each one's bounds (its
own collision ignored) measures the gap.

Args: labels: the actors (default every visible mesh actor). ignore: labels to skip (things meant to hang:
lamps, pictures). tolerance_cm: a gap over this is floating. max_check_cm: how far down to look.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"gaps": {label: cm or None}}}. Needs collision on what is underneath
(an object over a floor without collision reads as unsupported).
Example: film-ue op qa.floating 'ignore=["Pendant"]'

ops.name: qa.framing
ops.summary: How subjects sit in a camera's frame, measured from their bones (characters) or bounds (anything else).
ops.doc:
How subjects sit in a camera's frame, measured from their bones (characters) or bounds (anything else).

Args: subjects: actor labels. camera: a camera label; "" with sequence+frame: the cut's camera at that frame
(the sequence is scrubbed there first so animated cameras and bodies are where the shot has them).
expect: intent per subject or for all: {"size": "MCU"|["MS","MCU"], "headroom": [lo, hi], "side":
"left"|"right"|"center", "in_frame": 1.0}, or {"Ada": {...}, "Ben": {...}}. width_px/height_px: the output
aspect. still_out: also capture a still there with each subject's box and the problems drawn.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"camera", "subjects": {label: {size, box, headroom, eyes, looks,
look_room}}}, "still"?}. Multi-tick when sequence or still_out is given.
Example: film-ue op qa.framing 'subjects=["Ada"]' camera=CamA 'expect={"size":"MCU"}'

ops.name: qa.image
ops.summary: Exposure, clipping, colour and focus of a PNG on the box, as numbers and issues.
ops.doc:
Exposure, clipping, colour and focus of a PNG on the box, as numbers and issues.

Args: image: PNG path. subjects: {name: [x0,y0,x1,y1]} boxes (0..1; qa.framing returns them) for per-subject
brightness and focus. expect: intent, so a mood is not flagged: {"stops": [-3, -1]} mean exposure range in stops
from mid grey, {"cast": "warm"|"cool"|"neutral"}. limits: override thresholds (fmbridge.qa.metrics.LIMITS).
width_px: analysis size.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"exposure", "color", "regions", "subjects", "size"}}.
Example: film-ue op qa.image image=/tmp/qa/a.png 'expect={"stops":[-2,0]}'

ops.name: qa.overlaps
ops.summary: Actors whose bounds interpenetrate (a chair sunk into a table, two props in one place).
ops.doc:
Actors whose bounds interpenetrate (a chair sunk into a table, two props in one place).

Args: labels: the actors (default every visible mesh actor). ignore: labels to skip (the floor, walls, the
set's shell). ignore_pairs: [[a, b]] that may overlap (a book on a shelf). min_fraction: the share of the
smaller box that counts. touching_cm: resting contact allowed.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"pairs": [[a, b, fraction, depth_cm]]}}. Axis-aligned bounds: confirm a hit
with a still.
Example: film-ue op qa.overlaps 'ignore=["Floor","Walls"]'

ops.name: qa.parts
ops.summary: An actor's primitive components (names, classes, meshes, bounds): what to pass as body/garments.
ops.doc:
An actor's primitive components (names, classes, meshes, bounds): what to pass as body/garments.

Returns: {"label", "components": [{"name", "class", "mesh", "visible", "bounds": [origin, extent]}]}.
Example: film-ue op qa.parts label=Ada

ops.name: qa.penetration
ops.summary: Body showing through clothes, measured as the viewer would see it: two depth captures from each view (the
ops.doc:
Body showing through clothes, measured as the viewer would see it: two depth captures from each view (the
body parts alone, the garments alone); where a garment covers a pixel and the body is nearer by more than
`tolerance_cm`, skin pokes through.

Args: label: the character. body/garments: component names (default a MetaHuman's Body+Face / Torso+Legs+Feet;
qa.parts lists them), or labels of other actors whose meshes form that layer. camera: look from this camera (with sequence+frame: the shot's camera and pose); views: N
views around the character instead (or as well), at elevation_deg. size_px: capture size (square for views;
the camera's aspect otherwise). out_dir: write a still per view with the penetrating pixels painted magenta.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"views": {name: {fraction, pixels, worst_cm, box}}, "worst_fraction"}}.
Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op qa.penetration label=Ada views=6 out_dir=/tmp/qa/pen

ops.name: qa.review
ops.summary: Everything wrong with a shot, a sequence or a set, in one JSON and one picture.
ops.doc:
Everything wrong with a shot, a sequence or a set, in one JSON and one picture.

For each frame (sequence: `frames`, or `per_shot` per camera cut; no sequence: one still through `camera`) it
takes a still, measures exposure and colour, frames every subject (headroom, cuts, size), compares with
`reference_dir`/{frame:05d}.png when given, and (with "penetration") checks garments from the shot's camera;
once for the scene it checks floating and overlapping props; across cuts it checks exposure/colour continuity.

Args: out_dir: where frames, review.json and review.png go. sequence/frames/per_shot/camera: what to look at.
subjects: characters/props to frame (default every visible character). expect: per-subject or global intent
for qa.framing, plus {"image": {...}} for qa.image (e.g. {"image": {"stops": [-3,-1]}}). checks: a subset of
image, framing, penetration, floating, overlaps, continuity, reference (default all but penetration).
ignore: labels skipped by floating/overlaps (floor, walls). mode: still mode (view.still). baseline: a baseline
suite: each frame's still is checked against <suite>/<frame> (qa.baseline_check, `baseline_mode` auto: the first
run makes the baselines, later runs regress against them).
Returns: {"pass", "verdict", "counts", "summary": [lines, worst first], "issues", "metrics": {"frames"},
"report": review.json path, "image": review.png path}. Multi-tick; ~1 s a frame with mode=capture.
Example: film-ue op qa.review sequence=/Game/Seq/S010 out_dir=/tmp/qa/s010 per_shot=2

ops.name: qa.snapshot
ops.summary: The level's state as JSON for later diffs: every actor's class, transform, bounds, visibility, materials,
ops.doc:
The level's state as JSON for later diffs: every actor's class, transform, bounds, visibility, materials,
meshes, light and lens settings.

Args: out: also write it to this file. labels: only these actors.
Returns: {"actors": {label: {class, loc, rot, scale, bounds, hidden, mesh, materials, props}}, "meta"}.
Example: film-ue op qa.snapshot out=/tmp/qa/before.json

ops.name: render.cancel
ops.summary: Stop the render in progress (the chunk's frames so far stay; a re-run resumes).
ops.doc:
Stop the render in progress (the chunk's frames so far stay; a re-run resumes).

Returns: {"changed": bool, "was": status}.
Example: film-ue op render.cancel

ops.name: render.compare
ops.summary: Compare two renders frame by frame (two outputs of the same frames: a pre-rolled chunk against the full-shot
ops.doc:
Compare two renders frame by frame (two outputs of the same frames: a pre-rolled chunk against the full-shot
render, Linux against Windows, today against yesterday, a render against reference frames): per-frame SSIM and
PSNR, the worst frames, a pass/fail check at min_ssim, and optionally a sheet of the worst frames side by side.

Args: a, b: folders of frames named <frame>.<ext> (the beauty pass: <out_dir> or <out_dir>/FinalImage). frames:
[start, end) (default every frame in both). ext: png|jpg|exr. min_ssim: the pass threshold. worst: how many worst
frames to list (and sheet). every: compare every n-th frame. sheet: a PNG path for the worst frames side by side
(PNG frames). method: auto (ffmpeg ssim/psnr when the box has ffmpeg, else qa.compare at 480 px), ffmpeg or qa.
Returns: {"pass", "metric" (min SSIM), "threshold", "why", "mean_ssim", "min_psnr", "mean_psnr", "worst":
[[frame, ssim, psnr]], "below", "frames", "per_frame": {frame: [ssim, psnr]}, "method", "sheet"}.
Example: film-ue op render.compare a=/srv/r/full b=/srv/r/chunk 'frames=[1136,1160]' sheet=/srv/r/ab.png

ops.name: render.concat
ops.summary: Join video files of the same codec and size (chunks from several boxes, shots) into one without re-encoding,
ops.doc:
Join video files of the same codec and size (chunks from several boxes, shots) into one without re-encoding,
and optionally lay an audio file under the result.

Args: parts: video paths in order. out_file: the result. audio: a WAV/AAC to put under it. audio_offset_s: seconds
of that audio to skip.
Returns: {"path", "parts", "bytes", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op render.concat 'parts=["/srv/r/a.mp4","/srv/r/b.mp4"]' out_file=/srv/r/all.mp4

ops.name: render.describe
ops.summary: The render state for planning and for Claude: whether MRQ is rendering, the job in progress, and, given
ops.doc:
The render state for planning and for Claude: whether MRQ is rendering, the job in progress, and, given
out_dir (and name), the last report's summary and the frames on disk.

Returns: {"rendering", "status", "report": {...} | None, "frames_on_disk": int | None}.
Example: film-ue op render.describe out_dir=/srv/r/reel name=SEQ_Reel

ops.name: render.encode
ops.summary: Encode a render's frames into video with ffmpeg on the box: H.264 (yuv420p, CRF), H.265 or ProRes (prores_ks,
ops.doc:
Encode a render's frames into video with ffmpeg on the box: H.264 (yuv420p, CRF), H.265 or ProRes (prores_ks,
10-bit), with the render's WAV chunks laid on the timeline (or an audio file of yours). Frames must be complete
in the range; EXR frames are converted from linear with the sRGB curve.

Args: spec: the RENDER SPEC that rendered them. start/end: frames, end exclusive (default the spec's range).
outputs: video outputs (default the spec's h264/h265/prores outputs, else one h264).
Returns: {"videos": [{"kind", "path", "frames", "start", "end", "audio", "bytes"}], "changed", "fps"}.
Example: film-ue op render.encode 'spec={"sequence": "/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel", "out_dir": "/srv/r/reel"}' 'outputs=[{"kind": "prores", "profile": 3}]'

ops.name: render.frames
ops.summary: Render a few frames of a sequence through its camera cuts with MRQ, viewport-free (works offscreen on Linux):
ops.doc:
Render a few frames of a sequence through its camera cuts with MRQ, viewport-free (works offscreen on Linux):
for stills, contact sheets and checks (WP10's qa.still mode=mrq builds on it). Consecutive frames in one cut are
one MRQ job, pre-rolled from the cut start. Frames already on disk are reused.

Args: sequence: /Game/... level sequence. frames: sequence frame numbers. out_dir: directory on the box.
level: map (default the open one). preset: preview|draft|final|... width/height: pixels (default the preset's).
cvars: extra console variables. overwrite: render again even when the frame is on disk (out_dir shared with
other stills, or the scene changed since).
Returns: {"frames": {frame: png/jpg path}, "cameras": {frame: camera label}, "width", "height", "seconds",
"changed", "report"}.
Example: film-ue op render.frames sequence=/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel 'frames=[1200,1260]' out_dir=/srv/r/stills

ops.name: render.gpu
ops.summary: The render box's GPU and memory now: name, VRAM total/used/free in GB, utilisation, and the editor's RSS.
ops.doc:
The render box's GPU and memory now: name, VRAM total/used/free in GB, utilisation, and the editor's RSS.

Returns: {"gpu": {"name", "total_gb", "used_gb", "free_gb", "util_pct"} | None, "rss_gb", "rendering": bool}.
Example: film-ue op render.gpu

ops.name: render.job
ops.summary: Render a RENDER SPEC to the end (multi-tick: with --async the bridge returns a job id at once; follow it with
ops.doc:
Render a RENDER SPEC to the end (multi-tick: with --async the bridge returns a job id at once; follow it with
film-ue job ID, or render.status): plan the chunks, check the level and the GPU, render each chunk with MRQ (pre-rolled from its
shot start), watch frames, VRAM and stalls, then write <out_dir>/_render/<name>.report.json. Re-running resumes:
frames on disk (and complete) are skipped, so a finished job re-runs as a no-op.

Args: spec: the RENDER SPEC. stall_s: cancel a chunk after this many seconds with no new frame.
Returns: the report: {"status": ok|incomplete|failed|stalled|vram_abort|cancelled, "changed", "frames",
"seconds", "chunks": [{"id", "status", "frames", "missing", "median_s", "vram_peak_gb", "errors", ...}],
"measured": {"s_per_frame", "sample_s_1080p"}, "report": path, "errors"}.
Example: film-ue op render.job 'spec={"sequence": "/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel", "out_dir": "/srv/r/reel", "preset": "final", "shots": ["Reel_S16"]}' (or film-ue render job ... --async; film-ue render run SPEC)

ops.name: render.manifest
ops.summary: Write, per chunk of a spec, an MRQ queue manifest and the command line that renders it in a process with no
ops.doc:
Write, per chunk of a spec, an MRQ queue manifest and the command line that renders it in a process with no
editor (one process per job: survives editor restarts; run it on this box or another with the same project).

Returns: {"changed": True, "chunks": [{"id", "start", "end", "manifest", "argv"}], "exit_codes"}.
Example: film-ue op render.manifest 'spec={"sequence": "/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel", "out_dir": "/srv/r/reel", "executor": "cmdline"}'

ops.name: render.mrq
ops.summary: Start one Movie Render Queue job and return at once (poll render.progress); render.job does a whole spec.
ops.doc:
Start one Movie Render Queue job and return at once (poll render.progress); render.job does a whole spec.
Frames go to `out_dir` as {frame}.png|exr|jpg, the audio as a wav; `start`/`end` (end exclusive) render part of
the sequence. `preroll_from`: the shot's first frame when `start` is mid-shot: the frames between are evaluated
without rendering so cloth arrives as in a full-shot render (needs the camera cut to begin there). `executor`:
"pie" (in this editor) or "process" (a separate -game process; offscreen where the editor has no desktop). The
process loads the level from disk, and with unsaved changes the executor asks to save first: unattended, that
question goes unanswered and the job never starts, so unsaved packages are an error unless `save_dirty`.

Example: film-ue op render.mrq sequence=/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel level=/Game/Studio/Studio out_dir=/srv/r/s16 start=1196 end=1220

ops.name: render.plan
ops.summary: What a render spec would do, without rendering: the resolved settings, one chunk per camera cut (or per
ops.doc:
What a render spec would do, without rendering: the resolved settings, one chunk per camera cut (or per
