ops.name: seq.add
ops.summary: Make a level sequence, or converge an existing one's rate and playback range [start, end) (frames).
ops.doc:
Make a level sequence, or converge an existing one's rate and playback range [start, end) (frames).

Changing `fps` on an existing sequence keeps every key at its time in seconds (keys live in ticks); its
frame numbers change. `tick_resolution` migrates existing keys. Never opens a dialog.
Args: path: /Game/... . fps: 24, 25, 30, 23.976, "30000/1001". start, end: frames. tick_resolution: per second.
Returns: {"sequence", "created", "changed", "fps", "range", "tick_resolution"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.add path=/Game/Film/SEQ_010 fps=24 start=0 end=240

ops.name: seq.anim
ops.summary: Animation sections on an actor's skeletal mesh component (a MetaHuman's "Body" or "Face"), each
ops.doc:
Animation sections on an actor's skeletal mesh component (a MetaHuman's "Body" or "Face"), each
{"anim", "start", "end", "offset", "blend_in", "blend_out", "rate", "weight", "loop", "row"}: `start`/`end`
frames (end default: start + the animation's length / rate; past that it loops, `loop` False holds the last
pose), `offset` seconds into the animation where it starts, `blend_in`/`blend_out` frames of ease (weights
cross-fade where sections overlap: idle -> line -> idle), `weight` (1), `row` (default: the first free one; overlaps
go on separate rows). `replace` clears the track's sections first, else these are added. Returns [[anim, start,
end, row]].
Example: film-ue op seq.anim path=/Game/S/SEQ_A label=Host component=Body 'sections=[{"anim":"/Game/A/Idle","start":0,"blend_in":6}]'

ops.name: seq.apply
ops.summary: Converge a level sequence to a SEQUENCE SPEC in one call: create it, bind actors, write only the tracks that
ops.doc:
Converge a level sequence to a SEQUENCE SPEC in one call: create it, bind actors, write only the tracks that
differ (each track's keys batched), set markers; then describe again and confirm nothing is left to do.

Re-running with the same spec changes nothing (changed false). Tracks the spec does not name are kept unless
`prune`. A multi-tick job (big writes yield). See docs/unreal/sequencer.md for the spec.
Args: spec: the spec (dict). prune: bool. dry_run: plan only. save: save the asset.
Returns: {"changed", "steps": [{"op", "why", "result"}], "converged", "remaining": [...], "notes", "sequence"}.
Example: film-ue apply examples/unreal/sequence/two_shot.yaml

ops.name: seq.audio
ops.summary: Sounds in a sequence on a named audio track ("VO", "Score", "SFX"): clips [{"sound", "start", "end", "offset",
ops.doc:
Sounds in a sequence on a named audio track ("VO", "Score", "SFX"): clips [{"sound", "start", "end", "offset",
"volume"}] or [sound, start]: a SoundWave asset (assets.import a WAV first) from frame `start`, `offset` seconds
into it, to `end` (default: its length), at `volume` (1). For timing in the editor; the mix is made in post.
`replace` empties the named track first, else adds to it. Returns [[sound, start, end, row]].
Example: film-ue op seq.audio path=/Game/S/SEQ_A track=VO 'clips=[["/Game/Audio/L1",12]]'

ops.name: seq.bind
ops.summary: Bind an actor to a sequence by its label (a possessable), or make a spawnable the sequence owns.
ops.doc:
Bind an actor to a sequence by its label (a possessable), or make a spawnable the sequence owns.

spawn: {"class": "CineCameraActor"} or {"template": "<level actor label>"}; the binding is named `label`.
`replace` remakes the binding (its tracks go with it). Converges: an existing, bound binding is kept.
Returns: {"binding", "kind", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.bind path=/Game/Film/SEQ_010 label=Hero

ops.name: seq.camera_cuts
ops.summary: The edit: cuts are [camera label, first frame] in order; each runs to the next (the last to the end).
ops.doc:
The edit: cuts are [camera label, first frame] in order; each runs to the next (the last to the end).
Example: film-ue op seq.camera_cuts path=/Game/S/SEQ_A 'cuts=[["CamA",0],["CamB",72]]'

ops.name: seq.check
ops.summary: Numeric checks of a sequence: unbound bindings, camera-cut gaps and missing cameras, keys outside the
ops.doc:
Numeric checks of a sequence: unbound bindings, camera-cut gaps and missing cameras, keys outside the
range, rotation flips across +-180, overlapping shots, empty tracks.

Returns: {"pass", "issues": [{"code", "severity", "message", "fix", "frame", "subject"}], "metrics"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.check path=/Game/Film/SEQ_010

ops.name: seq.chunks
ops.summary: Render chunks that never start cloth cold: each lies in one shot and pre-rolls back to its shot's start.
ops.doc:
Render chunks that never start cloth cold: each lies in one shot and pre-rolls back to its shot's start.

Cloth (and any simulation) needs its history: a render that starts mid-shot is wrong (the Linux PoC's open
overshirt). Render [eval_from, end) and keep [start, end). max_frames > 0 splits long shots; max_preroll
caps the pre-roll (the chunk is then flagged "cold"); preroll adds frames before every shot start.
Returns: {"chunks": [{"start", "end", "shot", "shot_start", "preroll_frames", "eval_from", "first_after_cut",
"cold"}], "frames", "preroll_total"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.chunks path=/Game/Film/SEQ_010 max_frames=48 preroll=8

ops.name: seq.close
ops.summary: Close the open sequence.
ops.doc:
Close the open sequence.
Example: film-ue op seq.close

ops.name: seq.conform
ops.summary: Change a sequence's display rate, keeping either its TIME (every key, section and marker stays at its
ops.doc:
Change a sequence's display rate, keeping either its TIME (every key, section and marker stays at its
moment in seconds; frame numbers change; the default) or its FRAMES (frame numbers stay; the whole thing plays
faster or slower: animation rates follow, audio sections end where their sound does).

The tick resolution is changed too when the new rate does not land on whole ticks (29.97 / 59.94 need 60000),
with the keys migrated. `out`: conform a copy. A multi-tick job. Converges: the same fps again changes nothing.
Args: fps: 24, 25, 30, 23.976, 29.97, "30000/1001". keep: "time" | "frames".
Returns: {"sequence", "from", "to", "keep", "range", "tick_resolution", "off_frame", "notes", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.conform path=/Game/Film/SEQ_010 fps=25 keep=time

ops.name: seq.copy
ops.summary: Copy a sequence (all of it: the asset duplicated), or a window [start, end) of it moved to begin at `to`:
ops.doc:
Copy a sequence (all of it: the asset duplicated), or a window [start, end) of it moved to begin at `to`:
sections cut to the window (clips start that much later into themselves), curves holding their values at the
edges, markers inside kept. For pulling a shot out of a long sequence. A multi-tick job.

`replace` frees an existing `dst` first (no dialog), else an existing dst is an error.
Returns: {"sequence", "range", "tracks", "notes", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.copy src=/Game/Film/SEQ_All dst=/Game/Film/SEQ_sh020 start=120 end=240

ops.name: seq.cuts
ops.summary: The edit as it stands: [camera label, first frame, end frame] for each camera cut, in order.
ops.doc:
The edit as it stands: [camera label, first frame, end frame] for each camera cut, in order.
Example: film-ue op seq.cuts path=/Game/S/SEQ_A

ops.name: seq.describe
ops.summary: A level sequence as JSON: rate, range, markers, bindings (bound or not), every track with sections and keys.
ops.doc:
A level sequence as JSON: rate, range, markers, bindings (bound or not), every track with sections and keys.

The same shape seq.apply takes ("tracks"), so a describe fed back is a no-op. With `spec`, also "want": the
spec compiled against the level (look-at targets, clip lengths, property owners resolved) for planning
offline. `keys` False gives key counts instead of keys. `check` adds "lint" (seq.check's verdict).
Args: path: /Game/... sequence. spec: a sequence spec (dict). keys: bool. check: bool.
Returns: {"exists", "sequence", "fps", "tick_resolution", "range": [start, end), "markers", "bindings",
"tracks", "unsupported"(, "want", "notes", "lint")}.
Example: film-ue op seq.describe path=/Game/Film/SEQ_010 keys=false

ops.name: seq.diff
ops.summary: What differs between two sequences (`path` vs `other`), or between a sequence and what a spec asks for.
ops.doc:
What differs between two sequences (`path` vs `other`), or between a sequence and what a spec asks for.

Each track that differs says where first: a param, the section count, a section's range, a channel's key
(index, both keys). Args: path, other: sequences. spec: a sequence spec instead of `other`. tol: value tolerance.
Returns: {"same", "sequence": {fps/range/markers: {a, b}}, "bindings": [...], "tracks": [{"track", "change":
added|removed|changed, "where", "a", "b"}]}.
Example: film-ue op seq.diff path=/Game/Film/SEQ_010 other=/Game/Film/SEQ_010_v2

ops.name: seq.eval
ops.summary: What the sequence evaluates to at frames, without playing it: actors' world transforms (opens the sequence in
ops.doc:
What the sequence evaluates to at frames, without playing it: actors' world transforms (opens the sequence in
Sequencer: ControlRigSequencerLibrary evaluates the open one) and tracks' channel values (curve
evaluation; works closed). For checking keys landed where meant.

Args: frames: display frames. labels: actor labels -> [[x, y, z, pitch, yaw, roll], ...] per frame.
tracks: [{"kind", "binding", "component", "name"}] -> {channel: [values]}.
Returns: {"frames", "transforms": {label: [...]}, "channels": {track label: {channel: [...]}}}.
Example: film-ue op seq.eval path=/Game/S/SEQ_A 'frames=[0,24,48]' 'labels=["CamA"]'

ops.name: seq.key_collection
ops.summary: Key a scalar parameter of a material parameter collection (look.collection) on the sequence's track for that
ops.doc:
Key a scalar parameter of a material parameter collection (look.collection) on the sequence's track for that
collection: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...]. Sequencer writes the world's instance of the collection, so the
value reaches every material reading it with no mesh binding and no MID in between. Replaces only that
parameter's keys.
Example: film-ue op seq.key_collection path=/Game/S/SEQ_A collection=/Game/MPC_FM param=WipeOn 'keys=[[0,0],[24,1]]'

ops.name: seq.key_color
ops.summary: Key a colour property: keys [[frame, [r, g, b(, a)](, interp)], ...]. An FColor property (a light's
ops.doc:
Key a colour property: keys [[frame, [r, g, b(, a)](, interp)], ...]. An FColor property (a light's
"LightColor") takes sRGB 0-1, as look.light does; an FLinearColor one (fog "FogInscatteringLuminance", a post
"Settings.ColorGain") takes linear values. `srgb` overrides that guess. Component and replacement as key_float.
Example: film-ue op seq.key_color path=/Game/S/SEQ_A label=Key prop=LightColor 'keys=[[0,[1,0.8,0.6]]]'

ops.name: seq.key_float
ops.summary: Key a float property of an actor or component: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], interp "auto" (smooth,
ops.doc:
Key a float property of an actor or component: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], interp "auto" (smooth,
eased at held ends), "linear" or "constant" (stepped). `prop` is the C++ name or a path into structs, either
spelling: "Intensity", "Temperature", "FocusSettings.ManualFocusDistance" (CameraComponent), "CurrentAperture",
"Settings.AutoExposureBias" (a PostProcessVolume actor: set its override flag once with look.post), "FogDensity".
`component` by name or class ("CameraComponent", "LightComponent0"); "" = the actor if it has the property, else
its root component (a light's). `double` for a double property (a UE5 large-world value). Replaces only this
property's track on that binding; the keys hold before the first and after the last.
Example: film-ue op seq.key_float path=/Game/S/SEQ_A label=Key prop=Intensity 'keys=[[0,5],[24,10]]'

ops.name: seq.key_material
ops.summary: Key a material parameter on a mesh component's material slot (the material there must be an instance or
ops.doc:
Key a material parameter on a mesh component's material slot (the material there must be an instance or
material with that parameter): keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], a float for a scalar parameter or
[r, g, b(, a)] (linear) for a vector one. `slot` is its index or name ("M_Sheer"); `component` "" = the actor's
first mesh component. Replaces only that parameter's keys in the slot's track; other parameters keep theirs.
Example: film-ue op seq.key_material path=/Game/S/SEQ_A label=Sign param=Glow 'keys=[[0,0],[24,1]]'

ops.name: seq.key_transform
ops.summary: Animate an actor in a sequence: keys are [frame, [x, y, z], {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} | [x, y, z] to look at]
ops.doc:
Animate an actor in a sequence: keys are [frame, [x, y, z], {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} | [x, y, z] to look at]
with an optional 4th element, the interpolation leaving that key: "auto" (smooth, eases at held ends), "linear"
or "constant" (hold until the next key, a jump cut). `interp` is the default. Replaces the actor's transform
track (and only that), keeping the actor's scale; yaw is keyed as given, so unwrap it yourself across +-180.
Example: film-ue op seq.key_transform path=/Game/S/SEQ_A label=CamA 'keys=[[0,[0,-300,160],{"yaw":90}],[48,[100,-300,160],[0,0,150]]]'

ops.name: seq.key_visible
ops.summary: Show and hide an actor (or one of its components) over a sequence: keys [[frame, visible], ...], stepped; the
ops.doc:
Show and hide an actor (or one of its components) over a sequence: keys [[frame, visible], ...], stepped; the
first key holds before it. Overrides the level's hidden state while the sequence is open or playing (a
presenter hidden in the level can appear in the reel). `attached` keys the actors attached to it too (her
earrings and watch). Replaces only the visibility track.
Example: film-ue op seq.key_visible path=/Game/S/SEQ_A label=Prop 'keys=[[0,true],[100,false]]'

ops.name: seq.markers
ops.summary: Set a sequence's marked frames (replacing them): [{"frame", "label"}] or [[frame, label]], display frames.
ops.doc:
Set a sequence's marked frames (replacing them): [{"frame", "label"}] or [[frame, label]], display frames.

Returns: {"markers": n, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.markers path=/Game/S/SEQ_A 'markers=[[48,"beat"],[96,"hit"]]'

ops.name: seq.new
ops.summary: An empty level sequence for building into (no actor, no camera): playback [start, end) at `fps`. If it exists it
ops.doc:
An empty level sequence for building into (no actor, no camera): playback [start, end) at `fps`. If it exists it
is kept as it is (only its range set), so several scripts can each add their tracks; `replace` starts it afresh.
Example: film-ue op seq.new path=/Game/S/SEQ_A start=0 end=240 fps=24

ops.name: seq.plan
ops.summary: What seq.apply would do to converge the level's sequence to `spec`: the steps, nothing changed.
ops.doc:
What seq.apply would do to converge the level's sequence to `spec`: the steps, nothing changed.

Args: spec: a sequence spec. prune: also remove unlisted tracks of the bindings the spec names (default: the
spec's `prune`). Returns: {"steps": [{"op", "args", "why"}], "converged": bool, "notes"}.
Example: film-ue plan examples/unreal/sequence/two_shot.yaml

ops.name: seq.preroll
ops.summary: Give every shot / subsequence section of a sequence `frames` of pre-roll (and `postroll`): Sequencer then
ops.doc:
Give every shot / subsequence section of a sequence `frames` of pre-roll (and `postroll`): Sequencer then
evaluates each inner sequence that long before its section starts, so simulations have history at the cut.

Returns: {"sections": n, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.preroll path=/Game/Film/SEQ_Master frames=24

ops.name: seq.rebind
ops.summary: Point a sequence's actor bindings at the level's actors of the same label again, after the level was rebuilt
ops.doc:
Point a sequence's actor bindings at the level's actors of the same label again, after the level was rebuilt
and the old actors are gone (their tracks are kept; a binding removed and remade would lose them). `labels` None
= every actor binding whose name is an actor in the level. Returns {label: "ok" | "missing"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.rebind path=/Game/S/SEQ_A 'labels=["Host"]'

ops.name: seq.remove_binding
ops.summary: Remove an actor's binding (with its component bindings and all their tracks). Removing nothing is fine.
ops.doc:
Remove an actor's binding (with its component bindings and all their tracks). Removing nothing is fine.

Returns: {"removed": n, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.remove_binding path=/Game/S/SEQ_A label=OldCam

ops.name: seq.remove_track
ops.summary: Remove a track by identity: its kind, binding (actor label, "" = the sequence's own), component, and name
ops.doc:
Remove a track by identity: its kind, binding (actor label, "" = the sequence's own), component, and name
(property path, track name, "slot:N", collection path). Removing nothing is fine.

Returns: {"removed": n, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.remove_track path=/Game/S/SEQ_A kind=float binding=Key name=Intensity

ops.name: seq.retime
ops.summary: Move or stretch a sequence's time: f -> pivot + (f - pivot) * scale + offset, keys, sections and range alike;
ops.doc:
Move or stretch a sequence's time: f -> pivot + (f - pivot) * scale + offset, keys, sections and range alike;
or, with `start` and `end`, stretch only that span by `scale` and ripple what follows (a slow-motion beat).

`after` makes it a ripple (only what is at or after that frame moves: insert time with offset > 0, close a gap
with offset < 0). Animation sections play at rate / scale; audio is moved, never stretched. `out`: write to a
copy (made with the asset duplicated) and leave `path` as it is. Tracks of unsupported classes are not moved
(listed in "untouched"). Not idempotent: each call moves again. A multi-tick job.
Returns: {"sequence", "tracks", "notes", "untouched", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.retime path=/Game/S/SEQ_A offset=12 after=96
Example: film-ue op seq.retime path=/Game/S/SEQ_A start=48 end=72 scale=2

ops.name: seq.sample
ops.summary: Play a sequence frame by frame across editor ticks (so animation and rigs settle) and record bones' world
ops.doc:
Play a sequence frame by frame across editor ticks (so animation and rigs settle) and record bones' world
transforms, each [x, y, z, axis_x(3), axis_y(3), axis_z(3)], `camera`'s location, and `target`'s (see
seq.aim_point: a point, an actor, "Label:Component:bone"). A multi-tick job.
Example: film-ue op seq.sample path=/Game/S/SEQ_A actor_label=Host component=Face 'bones=["FACIAL_L_Eye"]' 'frames=[0,24]'

ops.name: seq.scrub
ops.summary: Open a sequence in Sequencer, locked to its camera, at a frame (for checking a pose in the viewport).
ops.doc:
Open a sequence in Sequencer, locked to its camera, at a frame (for checking a pose in the viewport).
Example: film-ue op seq.scrub path=/Game/S/SEQ_A frame=48

ops.name: seq.set_anim
ops.summary: Swap the animation on a component's track in a sequence: every section of it, or only those playing `only`.
ops.doc:
Swap the animation on a component's track in a sequence: every section of it, or only those playing `only`.
`label` picks the actor when several have a component of that name (both presenters have "Body").
Example: film-ue op seq.set_anim path=/Game/S/SEQ_A component=Body anim=/Game/A/Walk label=Host

ops.name: seq.shot
ops.summary: A shot: `anims` maps component names to animations ({"Body": idle, "Face": talk}); `audio` a SoundWave; the
ops.doc:
A shot: `anims` maps component names to animations ({"Body": idle, "Face": talk}); `audio` a SoundWave; the
camera cut on `camera`. Length: `seconds`, else the audio's, else the longest animation's.
Example: film-ue op seq.shot path=/Game/S/SEQ_A actor_label=Host 'anims={"Body": "/Game/A/Idle"}' camera=CamA seconds=5

ops.name: seq.shots
ops.summary: The shots of a sequence in order: its cinematic shot track's sections, else its camera cuts.
ops.doc:
The shots of a sequence in order: its cinematic shot track's sections, else its camera cuts.

Returns: [{"name", "start", "end", "sequence" | "camera", "preroll"}] (frames).
Example: film-ue op seq.shots path=/Game/Film/SEQ_Master

ops.name: seq.still
ops.summary: A still of a sequence at a frame through `camera`, or, with camera "", through the camera the edit (the camera
ops.doc:
A still of a sequence at a frame through `camera`, or, with camera "", through the camera the edit (the camera
cut track) shows at that frame: scrub there, let it settle `settle` ticks (temporal anti-aliasing, Lumen),
capture. A multi-tick job.
Example: film-ue op seq.still path=/Game/S/SEQ_A frame=48 camera=CamA out=/tmp/f48.png

ops.name: seq.stills
ops.summary: Stills of a sequence at many frames ({out_dir}/{frame:04d}.png): a contact sheet's worth in one call. Through
ops.doc:
Stills of a sequence at many frames ({out_dir}/{frame:04d}.png): a contact sheet's worth in one call. Through
one `camera`, or with camera "" each frame through its own shot's camera (the camera cut track): a previs of the
whole cut. A multi-tick job; returns [[frame, camera, path]].
Example: film-ue op seq.stills path=/Game/S/SEQ_A 'frames=[0,48,96]' out_dir=/tmp/sheet

ops.name: seq.time
ops.summary: Convert a time between frames, seconds, timecode and ticks at a sequence's rate (or `fps`).
ops.doc:
Convert a time between frames, seconds, timecode and ticks at a sequence's rate (or `fps`).

Args: value: 48, "2s", "48f", "1m30s", "00:00:02:00". fps: a rate (default: the sequence's, else 24).
Returns: {"frame", "seconds", "timecode", "ticks", "fps"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.time value=00:01:00:00 fps=23.976

ops.name: seq.tracks
ops.summary: What a sequence holds: for each binding (an actor, or actor.component) its tracks as [class, property or
ops.doc:
What a sequence holds: for each binding (an actor, or actor.component) its tracks as [class, property or
name, sections, keys]; master tracks under "". For checking what a build script made.
Example: film-ue op seq.tracks path=/Game/S/SEQ_A

ops.name: seq.validate
ops.summary: Check a sequence spec without touching anything: every problem at once, with where and what to write.
ops.doc:
Check a sequence spec without touching anything: every problem at once, with where and what to write.

Args: spec: a sequence spec (dict). Returns: {"ok", "problems": [...], "notes": [...], "tracks": [labels]}.
Example: film-ue op seq.validate 'spec={"sequence": "/Game/S/SEQ_A", "duration": "5s"}'

ops.name: seq.write
ops.summary: Write one canonical track (seq.describe's shape) into a sequence, replacing the track of the same identity.
ops.doc:
Write one canonical track (seq.describe's shape) into a sequence, replacing the track of the same identity.

Every key of the track goes in one call (batched, Sequencer closed while writing, a tick yielded every 2000
keys). Material and collection tracks replace only the parameters given. Bindings are made as needed
(possessables by label). A multi-tick job. Unchanged tracks are left alone (changed false).
Args: path: sequence. track: {"kind", "binding", "component", "name", "params", "sections"}. save: bool.
Returns: {"track", "keys", "sections", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op seq.write path=/Game/S/SEQ_A 'track={"kind":"float","binding":"Key","name":"Intensity","sections":[{"range":[null,null],"channels":{"value":{"keys":[[0,5],[24,10]]}}}]}'

ops.name: shot.apply
ops.summary: Shoot a shot list into its sequence: make or move each shot's camera (framed by the solver, the coverage or an
ops.doc:
Shoot a shot list into its sequence: make or move each shot's camera (framed by the solver, the coverage or an
explicit placement), key its moves, focal length and focus, and replace the sequence's camera cuts. Converges:
the same spec again changes nothing (force=True rewrites anyway); cameras the previous spec made that this one
drops are removed. A multi-tick job: the keys and cuts go in one batched seq.apply when WP8's core is there.

Returns: shot.plan's result plus {"changed", "cameras": {label: {"created", "keys"}}, "removed", "write"}.
Example: film-ue op shot.apply spec=@films/demo/shots/scene1.yaml

ops.name: shot.check
ops.summary: Check a sequence's edit numerically: every shot's frame (cam.check: QA's framing plus focus, safe areas,
ops.doc:
Check a sequence's edit numerically: every shot's frame (cam.check: QA's framing plus focus, safe areas,
dutch) at its start (or "middle"), and every cut (180-degree line, 30-degree rule). Scrubs the sequence: a
multi-tick job.

Returns: {"pass", "issues", "shots": [{"camera", "start", "end", "size"}]}.
Example: film-ue op shot.check sequence=/Game/Films/demo/Seq_Scene1 'subjects=["Host","Guest"]'

ops.name: shot.describe
ops.summary: The edit of a sequence as it stands: each cut's camera and frames with the camera's lens and pose now (its
ops.doc:
The edit of a sequence as it stands: each cut's camera and frames with the camera's lens and pose now (its
first key's pose is what the cut opens on when scrubbed), the size it gives on `subjects`, and the stored spec
hash.

Example: film-ue op shot.describe sequence=/Game/Films/demo/Seq_Scene1 subjects=Presenter

ops.name: shot.plan
ops.summary: Resolve a shot list against the level without changing anything: each shot's camera, frames, size, lens,
ops.doc:
Resolve a shot list against the level without changing anything: each shot's camera, frames, size, lens,
keys, the cuts, and every framing/cut issue. The dry run of shot.apply.

Args: spec: a kind "shot" spec (docs/unreal/camera.md; schema tools/filmtools/unreal/schemas/shot.schema.json).
Returns: {"sequence", "range", "cuts", "shots": [...], "issues": [...], "coverage", "spec_hash",
"up_to_date": whether the sequence already holds this exact spec}.
Example: film-ue op shot.plan spec=@films/demo/shots/scene1.yaml

ops.name: shot.sheet
ops.summary: A previz contact sheet of a sequence's edit: per shot 1 (its middle) or 3 (start, middle, end) stills
ops.doc:
A previz contact sheet of a sequence's edit: per shot 1 (its middle) or 3 (start, middle, end) stills
through the cut's camera, with thirds and safe-frame guides and a label (shot, camera, frame, focal), in one PNG.
A multi-tick job: about 2 s per still plus the drawing.

Returns: {"path": the sheet, "width", "height", "stills": [[frame, camera, path]]}.
Example: film-ue op shot.sheet sequence=/Game/Films/demo/Seq_Scene1 out_dir=/tmp/sheet per_shot=3

ops.name: speech.moods
ops.summary: The audio solver's moods (AUTO_DETECT, CONFIDENCE, EXCITEMENT, HAPPINESS, ...).
ops.doc:
The audio solver's moods (AUTO_DETECT, CONFIDENCE, EXCITEMENT, HAPPINESS, ...).
Example: film-ue op speech.moods

ops.name: speech.to_face
ops.summary: Import `wav` (a path on the workstation), solve it with MetaHuman Animator's audio solver in `mood` at
ops.doc:
Import `wav` (a path on the workstation), solve it with MetaHuman Animator's audio solver in `mood` at
`intensity`, and export an animation on `face_mesh`'s skeleton at {folder}/Anim/AS_{name}. A multi-tick job.
Then make it alive with perf.face (head, eyes, blinks, brows over the lip-sync).

Longer than `max_chunk_s` seconds: cut in pauses into chunks, each solved on its own (under {folder}/Chunks), and
stitched into the one animation. `timeout_s` per solve (0 = 60 s + 20 x the audio's length). A solve that fails
raises an OpError (code engine/timeout, with the reason) unless `fallback`: then that part becomes a lip flap
driven by the voice's loudness and the result says {"fallback": true, "errors": [...]}: re-solve when the solver
works.
Returns: {"sound", "performance", "anim", "pipeline", "frames", "seconds", "chunks", "fallback", "errors"}.
Example: film-ue op speech.to_face wav=/home/ue/Audio/line1.wav name=line1 face_mesh=/Game/MetaHumans/Ada/Face/Ada_FaceMesh mood=CONFIDENCE

ops.name: view.camera
ops.summary: Where things land in a camera's frame, without rendering: the camera as numbers, and world points or actors'
ops.doc:
Where things land in a camera's frame, without rendering: the camera as numbers, and world points or actors'
bounds projected to frame fractions (u right, v down, 0..1).

Args: camera: label ("" + sequence/frame: the cut's camera; the sequence is scrubbed there). points: {name:
[x,y,z]}. actors: labels (their bounds' screen boxes). width_px/height_px: the output aspect.
Returns: {"camera": {name, loc, rot, fov, aspect, focal?, sensor_width?}, "points": {name: {u, v, depth_cm,
in_frame}}, "actors": {label: {box, in_frame, area}}, "aspect_mismatch"?}.
Example: film-ue op view.camera camera=CamA 'actors=["Ada","Chair"]'

ops.name: view.overlay
ops.summary: Draw composition guides, labelled boxes and points on a copy of an image (no PIL needed).
ops.doc:
Draw composition guides, labelled boxes and points on a copy of an image (no PIL needed).

Args: image: PNG path. out: where the annotated copy goes. guides: any of thirds, safe (action 93% / title 90%),
center, golden, headroom, grid:4x3, aspect:2.39 (masks to that aspect). boxes: [{"box": [x0,y0,x1,y1] (0..1),
"label", "color": ok|info|warn|fail|[r,g,b]}]. points: [{"at": [x,y], "label"}]. caption: a text bar along the
bottom. width_px: shrink first (0 keeps the size).
Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "changed": true}.
Example: film-ue op view.overlay image=/tmp/qa/a.png out=/tmp/qa/a_g.png 'guides=["thirds","safe"]'

ops.name: view.sheet
ops.summary: A contact sheet from PNG files on the box: a grid of labelled frames in one image.
ops.doc:
A contact sheet from PNG files on the box: a grid of labelled frames in one image.

Args: images: paths. out: the sheet's PNG path. labels: one per image (default the file names). cols: 0 picks a
near-square grid. cell_width_px: each frame's width. title: a bar on top. statuses: ok|info|warn|fail per image
(a coloured border).
Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "cells", "changed": true}.
Example: film-ue op view.sheet 'images=["/tmp/a.png","/tmp/b.png"]' out=/tmp/sheet.png title=compare

ops.name: view.still
ops.summary: A PNG of what a camera sees, with no viewport.
ops.doc:
A PNG of what a camera sees, with no viewport.

Args: out: the PNG path on the box. camera: a camera actor label; "" with `sequence`+`frame` takes the camera
the cut shows at that frame; "" with `loc`/`look_at` [x,y,z] cm makes an ad-hoc camera (`fov_deg`, default 40).
sequence/frame: scrub the sequence there first (frames at its display rate). width_px/height_px: output size.
mode: "capture" (a scene capture: fast, ~0.1-1 s, no motion blur/DoF accumulation), "mrq" (Movie Render Queue
through render.frames: the final look, slower; needs sequence+frame and `level`), "viewport" (look.still's
high-res screenshot). warmup: captures before the kept one (temporal AA, Lumen). settle_ticks: editor ticks after
a scrub. hide: actor labels left out. guides: overlay guides drawn on a copy saved as <out>.guides.png
("thirds", "safe", ...). rt_format: capture mode's render target format (advanced; RTF_RGBA8, the default, or
RTF_RGBA8_SRGB, any case: a float target would export EXR, so it is refused; the selftest compares the two).
Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "camera", "mode", "frame", "camera_info": {loc, rot, fov, aspect},
"guides_path"?}. A multi-tick job.
Example: film-ue op view.still out=/tmp/qa/a.png camera=CamA width_px=960 height_px=540

ops.name: view.stills
ops.summary: Stills through a sequence's edit and a contact sheet of them: the whole cut in one picture.
ops.doc:
Stills through a sequence's edit and a contact sheet of them: the whole cut in one picture.

Args: sequence: the level sequence path. out_dir: where {frame:05d}.png and sheet.png go. frames: the frames to
take; None takes `per_shot` per camera cut (first, middle(s), last). camera: force one camera ("" follows the
cut). width_px/height_px/mode/warmup/settle_ticks: as view.still. sheet: also write sheet.png with each frame
labelled "frame camera". guides: drawn on the sheet's cells.
Returns: {"frames": [{"frame", "camera", "path"}], "sheet": path|None, "width", "height"}. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op view.stills sequence=/Game/Seq/S010 out_dir=/tmp/qa/s010 per_shot=2

ops.name: view.turntable
ops.summary: Stills of an actor from all around (a character, a prop, a garment) and a contact sheet of them.
ops.doc:
Stills of an actor from all around (a character, a prop, a garment) and a contact sheet of them.

Args: target: actor label. out_dir: where view_<yaw>.png and sheet.png go. views: how many, evenly around.
elevation_deg: the cameras' height angle above the target's centre. distance_cm: 0 frames the bounds with a
margin. fov_deg: horizontal. isolate: draw only the target (no set; lights still light it). start_yaw_deg: the
first view's direction from the target (0 = from +X, looking back at it).
Returns: {"views": [{"yaw", "path", "camera": {loc, rot, fov}}], "sheet", "center", "distance_cm"}. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op view.turntable target=Ada out_dir=/tmp/qa/ada views=8 isolate=true

ops.name: wp.describe
ops.summary: The open level's partition: whether it is partitioned, its editor and runtime bounds, how many actors it has
ops.doc:
The open level's partition: whether it is partitioned, its editor and runtime bounds, how many actors it has
and how many are loaded in the editor now, per runtime grid (data layers: level.layers).

Returns: {"partitioned", "editor_bounds": {"min", "max", "size_m"}, "runtime_bounds", "actors", "loaded",
"spatially_loaded", "always_loaded", "editor_only", "grids": {grid: count}, "loaded_by_ops": count}.
Example: film-ue op wp.describe

ops.name: wp.find
ops.summary: Actors of the partitioned level, loaded or not (from their descriptors on disk): filter by label substring,
ops.doc:
Actors of the partitioned level, loaded or not (from their descriptors on disk): filter by label substring,
class name, a box [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]] in cm, or loaded state.

Returns: {"partitioned", "count", "actors": [{"label", "guid", "class", "bounds", "grid", "spatial",
"editor_only", "data_layers", "loaded"}]} (the first `limit`).
Example: film-ue op wp.find contains=Tree loaded=false limit=20

ops.name: wp.load
ops.summary: Load part of a World Partition level into the editor: the actors whose bounds meet a box (cm), what a camera
ops.doc:
Load part of a World Partition level into the editor: the actors whose bounds meet a box (cm), what a camera
sees out to far_cm (its frustum, padded by pad_cm), what a sequence's cameras see through a shot (`sequence` with
`frames` [start, end) sampled `every` frames, through the camera cuts), a sphere around a point, named actors, or
everything. Waits (multi-tick) until they are in the editor world. `pin` also pins them.

Returns: {"partitioned", "changed", "requested", "newly_loaded", "already_loaded", "missing": [labels that did
not appear], "box", "cameras" (with sequence)}.
Example: film-ue op wp.load camera=Cam_A far_cm=8000

ops.name: wp.unload
ops.summary: Unload actors that wp.load loaded (by label, by box, or all of them). Actors loaded by the editor's own regions
ops.doc:
Unload actors that wp.load loaded (by label, by box, or all of them). Actors loaded by the editor's own regions
(or always loaded) stay: the library unloads only its own loads.

Returns: {"partitioned", "changed", "unloaded", "kept": [labels not loaded by wp.load]}.
Example: film-ue op wp.unload all=true
